questionText: (a) Give an account of the meeting between Elijah and Obadiah. [11 marks] (b) What two lessons can be learnt from the encounter? [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give an account of the meeting between Elijah and Obadiah. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What two lessons can be learnt from the encounter? [4 marks]

answer: (a) 1Kings16:29- 33;18:1-19: (i) King Ahab married a Sidonian princess, Jezebel, and brought her to Israel. (ii) She introduced the worship of Baal in Israel contrary to Israel's tradition. (iii) Elijah, the prophet, prophesied drought in Israel for three and half years as a result of Jezebel's apostasy. (iv) The drought caused severe famine in Israel. (v) As a result, Jezebel sought to destroy all the prophets of God. (vi) At this time, Obadiah, (the man in-charge of Ahab's household, hid and fed one hundred prophets of the Lord. (vii) Obadiah was sent by Ahab to search for water and grass in order to save the King's horses and mules. (viii) While Obadiah was searching for water, he met Elijah and prostrated before him. (ix) Elijah asked Obadiah to report his (Elijah) presence to Ahab. (x) Obadiah said he could not risk his life since Elijah could vanish from the scene at any time. (xi) Obadiah further told Elijah of how he had hidden and fed some prophets of God in a cave when Jezebel killed some of them. (xii) Elijah assured Obadiah that he was ready to meet Ahab and that he should be informed. (xiii) The king met Elijah and accused him of being the troubler of Israel. (xiv) Elijah counter-accused Ahab of being the real cause of all the woes of Israel. (xv) Elijah proposed a meeting at Mt. Carmel to settle who was the true God. (b) Lessons learnt from the encounter (i) Unfaithfulness to God attracts punishment. (ii) Punishment for sin brings untold hardship to both the innocent and the culprits. (iii) God has a way of solving human problems. (iv) People should be bold to confront those who cause human suffering. (v) God protects his people from harm. (vi) Believers should take care of God's people. (vii) It is good to discharge any assignment given by a true man of God. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) State the content of the New Covenant in (i) Jeremiah; (ii) Ezekiel. [10 marks] (b) Outline five benefits of the Covenant to Israel. [5 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: State the content of the New Covenant in

subQuestions.label: i
subQuestions.text: Jeremiah;

subQuestions.label: ii
subQuestions.text: Ezekiel. [10 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Outline five benefits of the Covenant to Israel. [5 marks]

answer: (a) (1) JEREMIAH 31:31-34: (i) This covenant would not be like the one He made with their fathers- the Sinai covenant. (ii) The people had broken that covenant. (iii) In the new covenant, God would put His law within them. (iv) He would be their God, and they would be His people. (v) The people would not need to be taught to "know the Lord". (vi) They would all know God, both great and small. (vii) He would forgive their iniquity, and would remember their sins no more. (2) EZEKIEL 36:25-28 (i) He would sprinkle clean water on them. (ii) He would cleanse them of idols. (iii) He would put in a new heart and a new spirit. (iv) He would replace the stony heart with the heart of flesh. (v) He would put his spirit in them and cause them to walk in his ways. (vi) He shall make them dwell in the land which he gave their fathers. (vii) They should be his people and he would be their God. (b) Benefits of the covenant to Israel: (i) God would gather Israel from countries that had taken them captives in God's anger. (ii) He would bring them back and make them dwell in safety. (iii) They would be His people; He would be their God. (iv) He would give them one heart. (v) He would make them fear God for ever for their benefit and that of their children. (vi) God would make an everlasting covenant with them and would always do them good. (vii) God would plant them in the given land in faithfulness with all His heart and soul. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) What did Jesus teach about any of the following during His sermon on the mount? (i) Earthly possessions; (ii) Anxiety. [10 marks] (b) In what five ways can the misuse of wealth lead to serious consequences for a nation? [5 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: What did Jesus teach about any of the following during His sermon on the mount?

subQuestions.label: i
subQuestions.text: Earthly possessions;

subQuestions.label: ii
subQuestions.text: Anxiety. [10 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what five ways can the misuse of wealth lead to serious consequences for a nation? [5 marks].

answer: (a) Matthew 6:19-34: (1) Worldly possessions: (i) Jesus taught his followers not to lay their treasures on earth where moth consumes and robbers steal. (ii) They should lay their treasure in heaven where it would be safe. (iii) For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. (vi) Jesus also said that the eye is the lamp of the body; thus if the eye is sound, the whole body would be full of light. (v) If the eye is not sound, the whole body would be full of darkness. (vi) Thus if the light in the body is darkened, then, the darkness is great. (vii) "No one can serve two masters" said Jesus; for either he would hate one and love the other. (viii) Or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. (ix) Jesus then concluded by saying that no one can serve God and mammon. (2) Anxiety: (i) Jesus taught that people should not be anxious about life; what to eat or drink. (ii) Or about their body, what they shall put on. (iii) According to Jesus, life is more than food and the body is more than clothing. (iv) He also said that birds neither sow nor reap or gather, but are fed by God. (v) Human beings, according to Jesus are of more value than birds. (vi) Jesus then asked, which of them, by being anxious can add a cubic to his stature? (vii) He wondered why they should be anxious about clothing. (viii) The lilies do not toil or spin, but are better arrayed than Solomon. (ix) God who clothes the grass will clothe them. (x) Jesus asked them to seek God's kingdom and His righteousness and all these things shall be added unto them. (b) Consequences of the misuse of wealth: (i) Earthly wealth is synonymous with mammon, thus if misused, it can lead to extreme poverty. (ii) Lack of concern for others and the nation doing evil. (iii) Pride and arrogance. (iv) Worship of materialism/worldliness. (v) Widening of gap between the rich and the poor. (vi) Oppression of the poor by the rich/greedy. (vii) National underdevelopment, famine, scarcity. (viii) Crisis and war. (ix) Anger of God. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Relate the encounter. between Jesus and the three would-be-disciples. [12 marks] (b) Mention any three demands of discipleship. [3 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Relate the encounter. between Jesus and the three would-be-disciples. [12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Mention any three demands of discipleship. [3 marks].

answer: (a) Luke 9:57-62: (i) On Jesus' way to Jerusalem, a man volunteered to follow him. (ii) Jesus told him that foxes have holes and the birds have nests. (iii) But the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head. (iv) Jesus then asked another man to follow Him. (v) But the man replied that he should be allowed to go and bury his father. (vi) Then Jesus said that the dead should be left to bury their dead. (vii) He went further that the man should go and preach the gospel. (viii) The third man said, "Lord, I will follow, but let me first bid farewell to my family" (ix) Jesus then remarked that no one who puts his hand on the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom. (b) Demands of Discipleship: (i) Total sacrifice (both physical and spiritual). (ii) Full commitment. (iii) Instant action, no delay/urgency. (iv) No distraction. (v) Complete loyalty to God. (vi) Not counting the cost and willingness to abandon everything else Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Narrate the story of the transfiguration [9 marks]. (b) Give three points of significance in this story. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate the story of the transfiguration [9 marks].

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give three points of significance in this story. [6 marks]

answer: Matthew 17:1-13 MARK 9:2 —15: Luke 9: 28 — 36: (i) Six days following Peter's confession, Jesus took with him Peter, James and John; (ii) to a high mountain (where he was transfigured before them). (iii) His face shone like the sun. (iv) And his garments became white as light. (v) There appeared to them, Moses and Elijah who talked with Jesus. (vi) They spoke about his death/departure. (vii) Peter suggested that he would make three booths — one for Jesus, one for Moses and the other for Elijah.. (viii) As he was speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them. (ix) And a voice from the cloud said, "This is my beloved son (with whom I am well pleased); (x) listen to Him". (xi) When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were filled with awe. (xii) Jesus came, touched them and urged them to rise and fear not. (xiii) When they lifted up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus. (b) Points of significance in the story: (i) The appearance of Moses and Elijah means that Jesus did not come to cancel the law and prophets but to fulfill them. (ii) The Transfiguration confirmed the divinity of Jesus Christ. (iii) The faith of the disciples in Jesus was strengthened. (iv) The appearance of Moses and Elijah confirmed the resurrection of the dead. (v) It also confirmed Jesus as the Messiah. (vi) The clouds signifies the glory/presence of God. (vii) Moses represented the Law and Elijah, the Prophets. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) What event led to the appointment of seven deacons in the early Church?[12 marks] (b) What three lessons can Christians learn from this episode? [3 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: What event led to the appointment of seven deacons in the early Church?[12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What three lessons can Christians learn from this episode? [3 marks].

answer: (a) Acts 6:1-6: (i) With the missionary activities of the apostles, believers increased in large numbers. (ii) The believers consisted of Hebrews and Hellenists. (iii) The early church lived a communal life involving distribution of items among the believers. (iv) The Hellenists complained that their widows were not attended to in the daily distribution of items (v) In consequence of this report, the twelve (the apostles) decided to separate the issue of food distribution from the issue of preaching the gospel. (vi) The twelve then called on the entire body of the believers/disciples to choose from among them seven men of repute to serve tables. (vii) These men should be full of the spirit and wisdom. (viii) Following the instruction of the apostles, seven men were chosen including Stephen and others. (ix) Their appointment was confirmed by the apostles through the laying of hands. (b) Lessons Christians can learn from the episode: (i) Need for communal life among Christians in the interest of love and unity. (ii) Christian should learn to take their complaints to the people of God rather than resorting to blackmailing. (iii) Christian should have standard in making appointment either in the church or in the society. (iv) Christians should be ready to serve in any capacity where they are called upon to do so. (v) Christians should avoid being covetous with regard to positions of responsibility. (vi) Christians should imbibe the culture of 'division of labour (vii) Christian should avoid court settlements. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) What was Paul's counsel concerning the use of spiritual gifts in the Church? [12 marks] (b) List three ways in which spiritual gifts are misused today. [3 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: What was Paul's counsel concerning the use of spiritual gifts in the Church? [12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: List three ways in which spiritual gifts are misused today. [3 marks].

answer: (a) Romans 12:3-8: (i) Paul advises that no Christian should think of himself more highly than necessary. (ii) But according to our level of faith, we should be sober while judging. (iii) Like the human body, we are severally gifted and do not have the same function. (iv) Since our gifts differ, we should use them according to the grace given to us and in measures to our faith. (v) All believers in Christ form one body (and are individually members of one another). (vi) If a member is a prophet, he should prophesy in proportion to his faith. (vii) Those given to service should be diligent in serving. (viii) Whatever the gifts, should be utilized to bless the body of Christ. (ix) Paul also called for cheerfulness in showing acts of mercy.. (b) Ways in which spiritual gifts are misused today: (i) Some regard themselves as superiors on account of their spiritual endowment. (ii) Some embark on self-glorification. (iii) They arrogate honour to themselves rather than to God. (iv) Some commercialize the gift of God. (v) Some feel it is their personal effort that fetches them the gift. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight the teaching of Paul on Christian giving as contained in Corinthians. [11 marks] (b) In what two ways can people benefit from giving? [4 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the teaching of Paul on Christian giving as contained in Corinthians. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what two ways can people benefit from giving? [4 marks].

answer: (a) 2 Corinthians 9:1-15: (i) Paul was grateful to the Philippian Christians for their gift and their continued concern for his welfare. (ii) Even in Thessalonica, they sent him gifts once and again. (iii) He was particularly happy that their support was to be renewed through Epaphroditus who volunteered to visit Paul and take gifts to him. (iv) The gifts were fragrant offering, a sacrifice pleasing and acceptable to God. (v) He was also happy that of all the Macedonian churches, none, except the Phillippian church, was prepared to enter into partnership with him in giving and receiving. (vi) He therefore prayed that God would provide their needs according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus. (vii) Paul was not ready to repeat his appeal to the Corinthians to contribute to the saints for he knew their readiness to do so. (viii) So he was proud of this and boasted of it to the people of Macedonia. (ix) He therefore sent Titus and other brethren as forerunners to arrange the collections in advance to avoid disappointment. (x) Paul said: He who sows sparingly will reap sparingly and vice versa. (xi) Each one must make up his mind not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver. (xii) He prayed God to give them in abundance so that they might have enough to provide for every good work. (xiii) He believed that the Corinthian Christians "would be enriched by God in every way for the great generosity which will produce thanksgiving to God. (xiv) He said that their offering would serve the needs of the saints who, in turn, would thank God on their behalf. (xv) He observed that by their generous donations, they had acknowledged the gospel of Christ. (xvi) And that the recipients would, in turn, desire to meet them while praying for them as God's grace had manifested in them. (b) Ways people can benefit from giving: (i) Joy of sharing with others — What God gives us freely, He expects us to share it with others. (ii) Christian should realize, like Paul, that it is more blessed to give than to receive. (iii) We should always give in appreciation that it was God who gave us all we have. When we give, it will be in appreciation of God's gift which is Jesus Christ. (iv) We are rewarded when we give. (v) God is never a debtor to anyone who gives. (vi) Our special talents/gift can be used in serving others to improve their situation in life. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Give Paul's teaching on "dignity of labour" in Thessalonians. [11 marks] (b) What four lessons can be derived from this teaching? [4 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give Paul's teaching on "dignity of labour" in Thessalonians. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What four lessons can be derived from this teaching? [4 marks].

answer: (a) 2 Thessalonians 3:6-15: (i) Paul commanded believers in the name of Jesus, (ii) that they should stay away from any Christian who lives in idleness, (iii) and any one who does not follow the tradition of hard work. (iv) They were expected to follow his example. (v) He was never lazy when he was with them. (vi) He never accepted food from anyone without paying for it. (vii) He worked hard, day and night to avoid being a burden to anyone. (viii) Although he had the right to be fed by them. (ix) He wanted to be of good example to imitate. (x) He gave the rule that whoever does not work should not eat. (xi) In the name of the Lord, Paul commanded the idle members to do their work; (xii) and earn their living. (viii) He asked the faithful to stay away from the idle one; (xiv) so that he will be ashamed. (xv) But he should not be seen as enemy. (xvi) But be warned as a brother. (b) Lessons to be derived from this teaching: (i) Laziness/idleness is to be condemned or avoided; laziness brings shame. (ii) Need for one to be self-reliant and not to be a parasite. (iii) Need for one to be proud of one's job. (iv) No particular job is more important or superior to others. (v) All jobs are complementary. (vi) Idleness can lead to downfall of the family, church and nation. (vii) Hard work makes it possible to help the needy. (viii) Looking down on certain jobs, especially the so-called menial jobs, is unchristian. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight James' teaching on faith and works.[11 marks]. (b) What two lessons can Christians learn from this teaching? [4 marks].

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight James' teaching on faith and works.[11 marks].

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What two lessons can Christians learn from this teaching? [4 marks].

answer: (a) James 2:14-26: (i) James began by questioning the profitability of a person's faith without works. (ii) He wondered how such a person's faith can save him. (iii) James also questioned profit gained when a Christian dismisses a needy brother without giving him the needed assistance. (iv) He asserted that faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead. (v) He challenged those who claim to have faith to show their faith without works. (vi) And he would show his works as a demonstration/manifestation of his faith. (vii) James warned that it is not enough to claim to believe in God; after all Satan also believes and shudders. (viii) He cited Abraham as a man justified by his works when he offered to sacrifice his only son, Isaac. (ix) James maintained that Abraham's faith was effective along with his works; (x) His faith was indeed perfected by works. (xi) Hence Abraham's belief in God was recorded to him as righteousness. (xii) James maintained that a man is justified by works and not by faith alone. (xiii) He also cited Rahab, the harlot, who was justified by her works for saving the spies. (xiv) He, therefore, concluded that faith without works is dead just as the body without the spirit is dead. (b) Lessons for Christians: (i) Faith in God is fundamental but does not rule out practical works. (ii) Christians have practical roles to play in realizing their dreams/destiny. (iii) God blesses people's works of faith and not faith alone. (iv) The best way to express faith and belief in God is to do what He says. (v) Faith without effective action results in failure. Previous

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight the main features of God's covenant with Abraham (b) State three reasons for covenant relationships.

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the main features of God's covenant with Abraham

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three reasons for covenant relationships.

answer: (a)Gen.17: 1 - 21: (i) At the age of 99,God appeared to Abram and asked him to walk before him and be blameless. (ii) God promised to multiply him exceedingly. (iii) Abram was to be the father of a multitude of nations. (iv) His name was changed from Abram to Abraham. (v) He would be made exceedingly fruitful. (vi) Nations and kings would come from him (vii) The covenant will be established between God and Abraham, between God and his descendants through their generations. (viii) God promised to remain his God and that of his descendants for ever. (ix) All the land of Canaan would be given to Abraham and his descendants. (x) Every male in his house should be circumcised on the eight day (he who is not circumcised would be cut off) (xi) The name of the wife Sarai was changed to Sarah (Mother of Nations) (xii) Sarah would be blessed with a son, Isaac. (xiii) Kings would come out from Sarah. (b) Three reasons for covenant relationship (i) For protection against enemies. (ii) To prevent infidelity / establish trust. (iii) To effect success in undertakings (iv) To wield influence. (v) To satisfy the demand of culture. (vi) To establish a relationship /friendship. (vii) To establish unity.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Explain the circumstances that led to the rejection of Saul as the king of Israel. (b) Mention two consequences of Saul's rejection as king.

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Explain the circumstances that led to the rejection of Saul as the king of Israel.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Mention two consequences of Saul's rejection as king.

answer: (a)Explain the circumstances that led to the rejection of Saul as the king of lsrael.1 Sam.15: 1 - 8: (i) God directed Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites. (ii) For opposing the Israelites on their way to the promised land. (iii) Saul attacked and defeated the Amalekites. (iv) But he spared Agag, the king. (v) He took spoil of the best of the (oxen, sheep, fatling and the lambs) (vi) He destroyed all that was worthless. (vii) God spoke to Samuel that He regretted having made Saul, king. (viii) For he had disobeyed His commandments. (ix) Samuel confronted Saul to register God's annoyance against him. (x) Saul defended self by asserting that he spared king Agag for sacrifice to God. (xi) Samuel asked Saul whether the Lord had any delight in burnt offering. (xii) That "to obey is better than sacrifice". (xiii) Samuel concluded that because Saul had disobeyed the word of God, the Lord had rejected him 1 from being the king. (b) Two consequences of Saul's rejection: 1Sam.16: 14-23; 31: 1-13: (i) Saul's kingship was taken away from him. (ii) The spirit of the Lord left him / He became mad / insane. (iii)An evil spirit came and tormented Saul. (iv) Saul and his three sons perished at the battle of mount Gilboa. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: a) Give an account of the report of the spies Moses sent to the land of Canaan.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Identify two lessons that can be drawn from this incident.

answer: (a)Give an account of the report of the spies Moses sent to the Land of Canaan: Num. 13: 17, 25-33. (i) At the end of forty days, the spies Moses sent returned. (ii) They brought back word to the congregation and showed them the fruit of the land. (iii) They reported that the land flowed with milk and honey. (iv) But that the people who dwelt in the land were strong, their cities were fortified and very large. (v) "They saw the descendants of Anak, the Amalekites, the Hittites, the Jebusites and the Canaanites. (vi) But Caleb quieted the people and said, "let us go up at once and occupy it, for we are well able to overcome it". (vii) But the men who had gone up with them said, "we are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than us". (viii) Ten of them brought to the people an evil report of the land they had spied. (ix) They claimed that the land through which they had gone was a land that devoured its inhabitants / that all the people they saw were men of great stature. (x) They also revealed that they saw the Nephilim (the sons of Anak who came from Nephilim) (xi) They reported that they were like grasshoppers before the Canaanites and were seen as such. (b) Two lessons that can be drawn from the incident: (i) We should be courageous to tell the truth always. (ii) A beautiful place could still have its challenges and flaws/pitfalls. (iii) It takes faith to believe you can be victorious when you face odds. (iv) Need to avoid inferiority complex. (v) Need for people to have high self image/ esteem. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Outline the main issues Jeremiah addressed in his prophecy of doom to Israel (b) Indicate two qualities exhibited by Jeremiah that is worthy of emulation.

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline the main issues Jeremiah addressed in his prophecy of doom to Israel

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Indicate two qualities exhibited by Jeremiah that is worthy of emulation.

answer: (a)Outline the main issues Jeremiah addressed in his prophecy of doom to Israel: Jeremiah 2,5: 14-19, 14:1-12. (i) According to Jeremiah, after the captivity in Egypt, God established a covenant with Israel to be their God, and they His people. (ii) While their fathers were faithful, the later generation were unfaithful. (iii) They forsook their. God who brought them out of Egypt and worshipped Baals. (iv) True religion was lost as the priests did not worship God, and prophets prophesied by Baal. (v) The law makers did not know God. (vi) Rulers transgressed against God. (vii) Israel had become a slave/servant/prey for others because they have forsaken God. (viii) The fear of the Lord was not in the Israelites, they did not serve the Lord but as harlots, went after other gods. (ix) This was in spite of the blessings God had showered on them. No amount of washing is able to make them clean since their sexual immorality was grave/ great. (x) As a result, Israel shall be put to shame for turning their backs on the Lord because they worshipped numerous gods. (xi) God's corrective measures had yielded no positive resuts. (xii) They killed their prophets, they killed the poor. (xiii) God's word will be fire and the people, wood, so that they are burnt. (xiv) God will bring a strong nation to punish Israel. (The nation will feed on Israel's food, flocks and herds, vines and fig trees). (xv) They shall destroy their cities and have Israel as servants. (xvi) Israel shall experience a great draught/no rain, no food for both humans and animals. (xvii) Even when they pray and fast because of their sins, God will not accept them /they will be punished. (xviii) Yet God will not punish them to the end / Jeremaiah preached hope to Israel. (b) Indicate two qualities exhibited by Jeremiah worthy of emulation: (i) He was an intercessor /good mediator (ii) He was a man of strong character (iii) He had a tender heart. (iv) He was a fearless prophet/ bold / courageous (v) He was asympathetic (vi) He had a reconciliatory spirit (vii) He had strong faith. (viii) He was optimistic. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Give an account of the Mission of the Seventy. (b) What two problems are encountered by evangelists today?

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give an account of the Mission of the Seventy.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What two problems are encountered by evangelists today?

answer: (a)Give an account of the mission of the seventy: Luke 10: 1-24: (i) Jesus appointed the seventy and sent them in pairs to every place He was to visit. (ii) Jesus emphasized that the harvest was plentiful but that the labourers were few. (iii) He asked them to pray that the Lord of the harvest would send labourers into His harvest. (iv) He sent them out like lambs in the midst of wolves. (v) He instructed them to carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, salute no one on the road. (vi) Jesus asked them to bless any house they entered. (vii) Jesus noted that their peace/ blessing would rest with such a house if a son of peace was there otherwise it would return to them. (viii) They should remain in the house,eating and drinking what was provided. (ix) The disciples were asked to heal the sick and preach the kingdom of God in every town they were received. (x) They were to shake the dust off their feet where they were not received. (xi) The seventy returned rejoicing that the demons were subject to them in the name of Jesus. (xii) 'Jesus said He saw satan fall from heaven like lightening. (xiii) He added that He had given the seventy authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions and nothing would hurt them. (xiv) They should, nevertheless not rejoice because the spirits were subject to them. (xv) But should rejoice because their names were written in heaven (b) Two problems encountered by Evangelists today: (i) Language barrier (ii) Financial handicap/constraint heaven. (iii) Lack of co-operation from catchment area/target audience (iv) Lack of broad knowledge of the scriptures (v) Hostility to the gospel/persecution (vi) Lack of conviction (vii)Cultural barriers (viii) Hostile geographical Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) What did Jesus teach about Himself as the True Vine? (b) In what three ways is this teaching significant to Christians?

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: What did Jesus teach about Himself as the True Vine?

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways is this teaching significant to Christians?

answer: (a)What did Jesus teach about Himself as the True Vine?: John 15:1-11: (i) Jesus said, "I am the true Vine and environment. my Father is the Vinedresser". (ii) "Every branch that is fruitless, He takes away! (iii) "Every branch that is fruitful, He prunes - to make it more fruitful". (iv) "You are already clean by the word spoken to you". (v) Abide in me and I in you". (vi) "The branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it abides in the vine. (vii) So you cannot bear fruit unless you abide in me. (viii) "If a man does not abide in me, he is cast forth as a branch and withers". (ix) "If you abide me and my words abide in you, ask whatever you will and it shall be done for you". (x) By this my father is glorified if you bear much fruit and prove to be my disciples. (xi) "As the Father has loved me so have I loved you, rem in my love". (xii) "These things I have spoken to you that my joy may be in you and that your joy may be full". b) Three ways in which the teaching is significant to Christians: (i) The Vine is the symbol of the relations) between Christ and believers (ii) The Christian is called to be fruitful. (iii) Unfruitfulness displeases the Lo (iv) Close fellowship with the Lord makes fruitfulness possible. (v) God's word enables us to abide in Him (vi) God wants our Christian life to be fruitful and joyful always. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Describe the mission of Peter in Lydda and Joppa . (b) State three lessons that can be learnt from this mission

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Describe the mission of Peter in Lydda and Joppa .

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three lessons that can be learnt from this mission

answer: (a) Describe the mission of Peter in Lydda and Joppa: Acts 9: 32-43: (i) Peter, at Lydda met Aeneas, bedridden and paralyzed for eight years. (ii) Peter said to him Aneneas, Jesus Christ heals you, rise and make your be (iii)Aneneas rose immediately and the people seeing it turned to the Lord. (iv) At Joppa, Peter met Tabitha who was full of good works and acts of charity. (v) She fell sick and died. (vi) Her body was laid in an upper room (vii) The disciples called for Peter to come and raise her. (viii) The widows were weeping, showing them the cloth she made for them. (ix) Peter came, putting all outside, knelt and pray for her recovery. (x) Peter then called her - "Tabitha arise", and she opened her eyes and sat up. (xi) Tabitha was presented alive to the church/people (xii) News of this spread throughout Joppa and many believed. (xiii) He stayed in the house of Simeon, a tanner for some days. (b) Lessons to be learnt from the mission: (i) The Healing ministry in the Church/power of God in healing (ii) members should be encouraged to care for one another as Dorcas was doing before her death. (iii) The pray ministry of the Church is of immense importance. (iv) The Gospel should be accompanied by signs and wonders (v) The Church should be a growing Church, with new believers being added each time. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight the story of the cleansing of the Temple in the Gospel of Matthew. (b) In what two ways is the Church defiled today?

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the story of the cleansing of the Temple in the Gospel of Matthew.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what two ways is the Church defiled today?

answer: a) Highlight the story of the cleansing of the Temple in the Gospel of Matthew: Matt. 21:12-17: (i) Jesus entered the temple and drove out all who sold and bought in the Temple (ii) He overturned the tables of the mon changers and the seats of those selling pigeons. (iii) He then said - 'My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you make it a den of robbers'. (iv) The blind and the lame came to Jesus in the Temple and He healed them. When the chief Priests and scribes saw the wonderful things he did (and the children crying out in the temple' Hosanna to David's son) they were angry. (vi) They said to Jesus, "Do you hear what they are saying? (vii) Jesus said, have you never read? Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou has perfect praise. (viii)And leaving them he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there. (b) Two ways the Church is defiled: (i) Through oath taking/ vow-taking. (ii) Through occult practices. (iii) Through breaking of commandments. (iv) Through unholy / ungodly association. (v) Through religious politics / Bribery and corruption. (vi) Through abominable acts (rituals and sacrifices). Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Outline the arguments used by Paul to defend the Resurrection. (b) In what three ways is the Resurrection signi-ficant to believers?

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline the arguments used by Paul to defend the Resurrection.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways is the Resurrection signi-ficant to believers?

answer: (a) Outline the arguments used by Paul to defend the Resurrection: 1 Cor. 15:1— 58: (i) The Corinthian Christians doubted the reality of resurrection from the dead. Paul therefore, explained to them the possibility of the resurrection of believers on the final day. Using the following arguments: (ii) He explained that since Christ died and resurrected, it meant that his followers would equally resurrect on the last day. (iii) He pointed out that Christ's resurrection was in accordance with the scriptures. (iv) It was witnessed by people including Cephas (Peter), the rest of the twelve apostles, more than five hundred brethren, James and all the apostles. (v)He also appeared to Paul, who was born late in apostleship because he was not one of the original apostles. (vi)He further explained that if Christ did not resurrect, they would not have been preaching that God raised Him from death for it would have been a mis-representation of God. (vii) Their preaching of the Gospel would have been in vain. (viii) Christian faith would have been futile. (ix) There would not have been hope for those who were dead in Christ. They would have died and perished in vain; and would have, among all men, been the most miserable. (x) But in fact, Christ has been raises from the dead, the first fruit of those who have fallen asleep. (xi) The baptism in the name of Christ would have not been necessary, as people could not have been baptized in the name of the dead. (xii) He Paul, would not have embarked on the missionary work that was full of danger and risk. (xiii) He would have encouraged people not to be mindful of morals, but to eat and drink, and be ready to die at any time. (xiv) He therefore warned the Christians not to be deceived by bad people who disbelieved the resurrection of the dead and thus ruined and discouraged good morals. (xv)As by one man death came, by one man also came resurrection from the dead. (xvi) The on of resurrection is Christ first, then the believers. (xvii) In a moment, in a twinkle of an eye, at the last trumpet, shall be changed. (xviii) For the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall be raised imperishable. (xix) This mortal body must put on immortality. (xx) Therefore, encourage one another with these words. (b) Three Significance of the resurrection to the believers: (i) It gives them hope that all believers will resurrect (ii) Believers will be able to see their loved ones again. (iii) Believers will have bodies, like Jesus' body (iv) Resurrection is the ultimate of Christianity. (v) With Resurrection, Christians are assured of life after death (vi) Death is not the end of everything but a transition. (vii) Therefore, no hopeless mourning. (viii) It confirms the divine nature of Christ. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Outline the features of the New Life in Christ as stated by Paul in Colossians. (b) State three practices which can have negative effect on Christian Community.

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline the features of the New Life in Christ as stated by Paul in Colossians.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three practices which can have negative effect on Christian Community.

answer: (a) Outline the features of the new life in Christ as stated by Paul in Colossians: Col. 3:1-17: (i) Christians are to set their minds on things above not on things that are on earth. (ii) They are to depart from all sinful practices e.g. fornication, impurity etc. (iii) And put on the new nature, which is renewed after its creator. (iv) They are to have compassion, kindness, meekness, and patience. (v) They are to forbear one another. (vi) Forgiving each other as the Lord has forgiven us. (vii) Put on love which binds everything together in perfect harmony. (viii) Let the peace of Christ rule our Hearts. (ix) Be thankful always (x) Let the word of Christ dwell richly in us. (xi) Teach and admonish one another in all wisdom. (xii) Sing Psalms and hymns and spiritual songs with thankfulness in our hearts. (xiii) Whatever is done in word or deed should be done in the name of the Lord. (b) Three negative practices that have effect on Christianity : (i) Gossiping and backbiting/quarreling. (ii) Greed and selfishness. (iii) Examination malpractices. (iv) Jealousy and envy. (v) Ritual sacrifices. (vi) Unforgiveness. (vii) Covetousness and stealing. (viii) Bribery and corruption (ix) Sexual immorality. (x) Alcoholism. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight Peter's advice to Christians living among non-Christians (b) In what three ways can Christians promote good relationship with non-Christians?

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight Peter's advice to Christians living among non-Christians

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways can Christians promote good relationship with non-Christians?

answer: (a) Highlight Peter's advice to Christians living among non-Christians: 1 Peter 2:9— 25: (i) Peter advised that Christians should abstain from the passion of the flesh . (ii) Maintain good conduct among the Gentiles. (iii) If they speak against them as wrong doers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God. (iv) They should be subject to every human institution i.e. to the Emperor or to Governors who have power to punish or praise. (v) By doing right, they would silence the ignorance of foolish-men. (vi) They should live as free men but do not use their freedom as pretext for evil. (vii) They should live as servants of God. (viii) Honour all men (ix) Love the brotherhood (x) Fear God. (xi) Honour the Emperor. (b) Three ways to promote good relationship: (i) Participation in community development projects with non Christians. (ii) Contribution towards the needs of non-Christians. (iii) Participation in social activities with non-Christians. (iv)Accommodation of programmes and activities of non-Christians. (v) Acceptance of non-Christians in Christian institution e.g. schools. (vi) Attendance at programmes of non-Christians. (vii) Educative interaction about other religions. (viii) Religious tolerance. (ix) Being well informed about the other religions. (x) Showing good examples /Being role models. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) According to Peter, what should be the Christian attitude in the face of persecution? (b) State three types of persecution Christians may encounter today

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: According to Peter, what should be the Christian attitude in the face of persecution?

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three types of persecution Christians may encounter today

answer: (a) According to Peter what should be the Christian attitude in the face of persecution?: 1 Peter 4:12— 19: (i) According to Peter, Christians should not be surprised at every fiery ordeal, which comes to them. (ii) They should not see it as a strange happening to them. (iii)They should rejoice as in it they share Christ's sufferings. (iv) They should rejoice and be glad when Christ's glory is revealed. (v) If they are reproached for Christ's name they are blessed. (vi) The spirit of glory and God rests upon you. (vii) They should never suffer as murderers or thieves. (viii) Never suffer as a wrong doer or mischief-maker. (ix) He advised that if they suffer as Christians, they should not be ashamed. (x) Under the name of Jesus, they should glorify God. (xi) It is time for judgment to begin from God's household. (xii) The fate for those who do not obey God will be worse. (xiii) Those who suffer according to God's will should do right. (xiv) They should entrust their souls to a faithful creator. (b) Three types of Persecution Christians encounter today: (i) The state restricting their use of the Media such as Radio/Television. (ii) Discrimination in job and scholarship allocation. (iii) Prohibition of open air rallies/crusades. (iv) Taking over or undue interference in Christian institutions. (v) Disturbance of worship services. (vi) Withholding of privileges e.g. acquiring of state lands. (vii) Injustice in the courts. Previous

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) How did Moses become the son of Pharaoh's daughter? [9 marks] (b) Explain in three ways how this prepared Moses for his future leadership roles. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: How did Moses become the son of Pharaoh's daughter? [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Explain in three ways how this prepared Moses for his future leadership roles. [6 marks]

answer: (a) Exodus 1, 2:1-10 (i) A new Pharaoh who did not know Joseph arose over Egypt. (ii) He feared that Israel, given their large population, could ally with other nations against Egypt. (iii) He decided to enslave Israel; hence, task masters were set over them to afflict them with heavy burdens. (iv) Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah to kill every male baby of the Hebrew women at birth. (v) The midwives feared God and did not obey Pharaoh's order. (vi) Moreover, the Hebrew women were stronger - before the nurse came, they gave birth. (vii) Then Pharaoh commanded all his people to cast every son born to the Hebrews in the Nile, but to spare only daughters. (viii) Moses was born to a Hebrew couple of the Levite family. (ix) When after three months, his mother could no longer hide him, she dropped him in a basket by the Nile. (x) Pharaoh's daughter picked the young Moses. (xi) She contracted Moses' biological mother (unknowingly though) to nurture and bring up the boy for her. (xii) Moses' mother nursed him and when he grew she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter and he became her son. (xiii) She named him Moses meaning, I drew him out of water'. (b) Three ways Moses was prepared for leadership roles: (i) Royal upbringing gave him advantage of good education. (ii) Familiarization with the machinery of government/administration. (iii) Appreciation of sufferings of his people. (iv) Patriotism and love for his people. (v) Being conversant with the culture of his people.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: a) Narrate the story of David's sin against Uriah. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What two lessons can Christians learn from this incident? [4 marks]

answer: 2 Samuel 11: 1 - 27; 12: 1 - 15: (i) During the war with the Ammorites, David did not go to war. (ii) He was strolling on the top of his roof and saw a beautiful woman having her bath. (iii) David inquired about her and he was told that she was Bath-Sheba, (daughter of Eliam). (iv) The wife of Uriah, the Hittite. (v) David sent for her and slept with her. (vi) She went home and later informed David that she was pregnant. (vii) David invited the husband from the battlefield to sleep with Bath-Sheba. (viii) But Uriah refused saying that it was against Isralite custom to leave the battlefield when the war was in progress. (ix) As a result, he was sent to the hottest part in the war front. (x) And Uriah was killed. (xi) After Bath-Sheba had mourned her late husband, David brought her into his house and married her. (xii) Prophet Nathan condemned the attitude of David through a parable. (xiii) He told him about God's punishment . (xiv) David regretted his actions, repented and confessed his guilt. (xv) God forgave him. (b) Two lessons Christians can learn from this incident: (i) Christians should avoid adultery. (ii) Sin attracts punishment. (iii) Sin causes separation between man and God. (iv) When Christians acknowledge their guilt and repent, there is always an avenue for forgiveness. (v) A Christian should not kill or covet his/her neighbour's things. vi) A Christian should be patriotic/loyal. (vii) Nothing is hidden from God. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Describe king Nebuchadnezzar's attack on Judah. [11 marks] (b) List four effects of war on a nation.[4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Describe king Nebuchadnezzar's attack on Judah. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: List four effects of war on a nation.[4 marks]

answer: (a) 2Kings 24:10 17; 25:1 — 17: (i) As King Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, King Jehoiachin surrendered his administration to him. (ii) The King of Babylon carried away all the treasures in the King's house. (iii) All the vessels of gold in the temple were destroyed. (iv) Able bodied people of Jerusalem (i.e. the princes, mighty men of valour and thousands of captives) were carried away. (v) He carried away King Jehoiachin and his household to Babylon. (vi) He left behind the poorest of the land. (vii) He appointed Mattaniah King and renamed him Zedekiah. (viii) Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon and this led to another round of siege on the city this eventually brought famine. (ix) Zedekiah, who escaped, was overtaken and arrested. (x) He was brought to the King of Babylon where his two sons were killed in his presence. (xi) Nebuzaradan came to set the house of the Lord on fire, including the king's house and other houses in Jerusalem. (xii) The army of the Chaldeans led by the captain of the guard broke down walls around Jerusalem and carried captives to Babylon. (xiii) Some of the people left in the land were vinedressers and ploughmen. (xiv) Some precious material (i.e. pillars of bronze, the stands and bronze sea) were destroyed. (xv) But the pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes, incense, vessels of bronze, fine pan, gold and silver materials were carried away to Babylon. (b) Four effects of war on a nation: (i) Bitterness (ii) Famine (iii) Distrust (iv) Enmity (v) Suspicion (vi) Calamity (vii) Loss of life and property (viii) Poverty (ix) Disunity/disorderliness/unrest (x) Underdevelopment (xi) Death/ destruction of lives Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) State three criticisms Isaiah made against Israel's system of worship. [6 marks] (b) What three suggestions did Isaiah give for Israel's return to God? [6 marks] (c) In what three ways can your country return to God. [3 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: State three criticisms Isaiah made against Israel's system of worship. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What three suggestions did Isaiah give for Israel's return to God? [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: c
subQuestions.text: In what three ways can your country return to God. [3 marks]

answer: (a) Isaiah 1 : 10 — 20: Isaiah said that: (i) their sacrifices were meaningless. (ii) God was fed up with their burnt offerings of ram and beast. (iii) God was not delighted in the blood of bulls and lambs. (iv) they perverted justice. (v) their new moon and Sabbath He hated. (vi) their offering was vain. (vii) their incense was an abomination. (b) (i) They should wash and be clean by removing evil from their doing/ casting away idols. (ii) They should cease to do evil and learn to do good. (iii) They should seek justice, correct oppression. (iv) They should defend the fatherless and plead for the widow. (v) They should come to God and confess their sins so that they can be as white as snow total commitment to God. (vi) If they were willing and obedient, they would eat the good of the land. (vii) But if they refused, they would be devoured. (c) Three ways our country can return to God: (I) Fighting the cause of the poor. (ii) Having true repentance. (iii) Asking for forgiveness. (iv) Praying and fasting. (v) Serving God whole heartedly. (vi) Forsaking sin and amending ways. (vii) Punishing injustice and anti-social behaviour. (viii) Encouraging good behaviour with reward. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Narrate Jesus' encounter with the Gerasene demoniac. [11 marks] (b) In what two ways can the society improve the conditions of mental patients? [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate Jesus' encounter with the Gerasene demoniac. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what two ways can the society improve the conditions of mental patients? [4 marks]

answer: (a) Mark 5:1 — 20: (i) Coming out of the boat at Gerasene, a demoniac came out of the tomb to meet Jesus. (ii) Nobody could bind the man even with fetters and chains, which he often broke into pieces. (iii) No one could also subdue or tame the man. (iv) The demoniac spent night and day among the tombs on mountain, bruising himself with stones. (v) When he saw Jesus at a distance, he ran and worshipped him. (vi) With a loud voice, he said, 'what have you to do with me Jesus — son of the Most High God? (vii) The demoniac begged Jesus not to torment him. (viii) Jesus had earlier ordered the unclean spirit to get out of the man. (ix) Jesus asked for his name. (x) The demoniac declared that he was 'Legion', meaning that many unclean spirits were controlling him. (xi) On request, the unclean spirits were sent into the nearby swine (numbering about two thousand). (xii) The swine rushed and drowned in the sea. (xiii) The herdsmen were surprised and fled to declare what they witnessed in the city. (xiv) The former demoniac was found at the feet of Jesus well clothed in his right mind, (this was to the people's dismay). (xv) They began to beg Jesus to depart from their neighbourhood. (xvi)As he was departing by boat, the man who had been cured wanted to follow Jesus. (xvii) Instead, Jesus asked him to go home to his friends and tell them what God had done for him. (xviii) This act was publicized. (b) Two ways the Society can improve the condition of mental patients: (i) Improving basic facilities in psychiatric hospital. (ii) Training of specialist psychiatrists. (iii) Subsidizing drugs for the patients. (iv) Showing love and concern. (v) Formation of NGOs to care for them. (vi) Building of rehabilitation centres. (vii) Making provision for counseling services/centres Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Narrate the trial of Jesus before Pilate and the Roman authorities as recorded in Matthew. [11 marks] (b) Give two reasons why Pilate was wrong for condemning Jesus to death. [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate the trial of Jesus before Pilate and the Roman authorities as recorded in Matthew. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give two reasons why Pilate was wrong for condemning Jesus to death. [4 marks]

answer: (a) Mathew 27: 11 — 31: (i) The governor asked Jesus if he was the King of the Jews. (ii) He answered, 'You have said so'. (iii) Jesus did not respond to the allegations of the priest and elders, not even to a single charge. (iv) It was customary that the governor should release to the crowd any prisoner they wanted at the feast. (v) Pilate asked whom they wanted released to them, Jesus or Barabbas? (vi) Pilate knew they delivered Jesus for judgement out of envy. (vii) His wife had also warned him not to have a hand in the death of Jesus. (viii) The Chief Priest and the elders persuaded the people to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus. (ix) Pilate asked them , again, 'whom they wanted released to them'. (x) They unanimously demanded for the release of Barabbas and that Jesus be crucified. (xi) Pilate washed his hands before the crowd and declared, 'I an innocent of this man's blood, see to it yourselves.' (xii) All the people said, 'His blood be on us and our children!' (xiii) Pilate released Barabbas; and having scourged Jesus, delivered him to be crucified. (xiv) The soldiers led Jesus into the Praetorium stripped him, put a scarlet robe on him and a crown of thorns on his head and a reed in his right hand. (xv) Kneeling before him, the soldiers mocked him saying, 'Hail, King of the Jews!. (xvi) They spat on him, took t reed and struck him on the head. (xvii) They removed the robe, put his own clothes on him and led him away crucify him. (b) Two reasons why Pilate was wrong for condemning Jesus: (i) Pilate presented himself as a weak leader. (ii) He was pleasing the people to keep his job/position. (iii) Pilate knew that Jesus was truly innocent of the charges. (iv) His own wife sent word to him to have nothing to do with the righteous man. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Describe Philip's missionary activities in Judea and Samaria. [9 marks] (b) State three problems facing the work of evangelism in your country. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Describe Philip's missionary activities in Judea and Samaria. [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three problems facing the work of evangelism in your country. [6 marks]

answer: (a) Acts 8:26 — 40: (i) A great persecution arose against the church in Jerusalem after the death of Stephen. (ii) Those who scattered went about preaching the word. (iii) Philip went down to Samaria and proclaimed Christ. (iv) A great number of people believed when they heard Philip and saw the signs performed. (v) Those who believed the good news about the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ were baptized. (vi) Simon, the magician, who had for long amazed the people with his magical powers, was also baptized having believed. (vii) The Apostles in Jerusalem sent Peter and John who came down and prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit. (viii) They laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Spirit. (ix) Simon offered money to be given the power to lay hands on people. (x) Peter rebuked his evil motives and request, asking him to repent that the intent of his heart be forgiven him. (xi) But an angel of the Lord directed Philip to the road that goes from Jerusalem to Gaza. (xii) Here, he met an Ethiopians eunuch, a minister of the Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who had come to Jerusalem to worship and was returning. (xiii) Led by the spirit, Philip joined the eunuch in his chariot, explained the word of God to him; and he repented and believed. (xiv)As they went along the road, they saw water and the eunuch requested to be baptized, and was baptized. (b) Three problems facing Evangelism: (i) Religious conflict/Political instability. (ii) Materialism/worldliness. (iii) Financial problem. (iv) Lack of commitment. (v) Limited knowledge of the word/scripture. (vi) Modernity (vii) False teaching (viii) Political interference. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Describe the healing of the man by the pool called Bethzatha. [11 marks] (b) State two reasons why Jesus performed healing miracles. [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Describe the healing of the man by the pool called Bethzatha. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State two reasons why Jesus performed healing miracles. [4 marks]

answer: (a) John 5: 2-18: (i) In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, was a pool which, in Hebrew, is called Bethsaida, where many invalids (sick people, blind, lame and paralysed) rushed into it to be healed. (ii) One of the paralyzed was a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years. (iii) Jesus saw him and knew that the man had been lying there for a long time. (iv) Jesus asked him 'Do you want to be healed?. (v) The man replied that he had no man to carry him into the pool when the water was troubled. (vi) And other often got there before him. (vii) Jesus commanded the man, 'Rise, take up your pallet, and walk'. (viii) And the man was healed immediately. (ix) He took up his pallet and walked. (x) The Jews began to argue with the man that since it was Sabbath, it was not lawful for man to carry his pallet. (xi) The man replied the critics that the man who healed him only directed him to take up his pallet and walk. (xii) The Jews asked the man about the identity of the person who healed him. (xiii) The man could not ascertain the identity of Jesus since He had, withdrawn. (xiv) Later, Jesus met the man in the temple and said to him, 'See, you are well! Sin no more, that nothing worse befall you'. (xv) The healed man went and told the Jews that it was Jesus who healed him. (xvi) There, the Jews persecuted Jesus. (xvii) Jesus asserted, `My father is working still, and I am working'. (xviii) For breaking the Sabbath and calling God his Father, thus equating himself with God, the Jews pressed further to kill him. (b) Two reasons why Jesus performed healing miracles: (i) Out of compassion (ii) Out of love (iii) Out of his divine nature (iv) Out of necessity (v) To destroy the work of darkness/enemy (vi) To save or deliver mankind (vii) To show his authority as son of God (viii) To make people believe. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Outline the qualities of a New Life in Christ as contained in Paul's letter to the Colossians. [11 marks] (b) List four qualities of a genuine Christian. [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline the qualities of a New Life in Christ as contained in Paul's letter to the Colossians. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: List four qualities of a genuine Christian. [4 marks]

answer: Colossians 3:1-17: (a) (i) Seeking the things that are above where Christ is, seated at the right of God. (ii) Setting one's mind on things that are above so as to appear with Christ in his glory. (iii) Putting to death things that are earthly in one's body (i.e. fornication, impurity, passion, evil desire and covetousness) which is idolatry. (iv) Putting away anger, wrath, malice, slander, foul talk from one's mouth and lying to one another. (v) The new nature is being renewed in knowledge after the image of its creator. (vi) No discrimination (i.e Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, freeman) but Christ is all in all. (vii) As God's chosen ones, Christians are to put on compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness and patience. (ix) Forbearing one another; and if offended, there should be immediate forgiveness as the Lord forgives. (x) Putting on love, peace of Christ rules in one's heart. (xi) The word of Christ dwells in one richly. (xii) Teaching and admonishing one another in all wisdom. (xiii) Singing psalms and hymns as well as spiritual songs with thankfulness. (xiv) Saying and doing everything in the name of the Lord Jesus giving thanks to God the Father through him. (b) Four qualities of a genuine Christian: A genuine Christian (i) is spiritually oriented. (ii) does not discriminate against people. (iii) loves all and sundry. (iv) endures suffering and difficult times. (v) exhibits the fruits of the spirit. (vi) is fervent in spirit. (vii) has a forgiving spirit. (viii) is not worldly. (ix) is regenerated. (x) is obedient to God's commandment. (xi) gives to the needy. (xii) should be involved in evangelism. (xiii) should fellowship with other Christians. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight Paul's advice to the Thessalonian Christians on the matter of idleness. [9 marks] (b) State three consequences of idleness in the society. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight Paul's advice to the Thessalonian Christians on the matter of idleness. [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three consequences of idleness in the society. [6 marks]

answer: (a) Thessalonians 3:6-15: (i) Paul commanded the brethren in the name of Jesus to keep.away from a brother who was living in idleness. (ii) Not in accordance with the tradition of hardwork and industry which they received from the Apostles. (iii) They ought to imitate the Apostles, since they were not idle when they were with the Thessalonians. (iv) The disciples did not eat from the Thessalonians without paying. (v) They laboured and toiled, night and day, that they might not burden the Thessalonian Christians. (vi) Though it was their right to depend on the Thessalonians, yet they decided to be self-dependent. (vii) In order to show their conduct as an example to imitate. (viii) Paul had earlier given the Thessalonians an instruction that whoever would not work should not be allowed to eat. (ix) News had reached Paul and other Apostles that they were mere busy bodies, doing nothing. (x) Such persons were exhorted in the Lord to do their work in quietness, to earn their own living. (xi) They should note that anyone who refuses to obey the instructions in the letter should be disassociated with. (xiii) The Thessalonians should not look upon him as an enemy but warn him as a brother. (b) Three consequences of idleness in the Society: (i) Stealing/Robbery (ii) Disaffection (iii) Quarrel (iv) Laziness (v) Peddling of rumour (vi) Drunkenness (vii) Sexual immorality and its attendant problems (viii) Physical weakness of the body (ix) Bitterness (x) Underdevelopment (xi) Depending on others (xii) Thuggery (xiii) Nonentity/nuisance Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Explain Paul's teaching that Christians are children of God through Christ. [12 marks] (b) Give three implications of this doctrine of sonship of God. [3 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Explain Paul's teaching that Christians are children of God through Christ. [12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give three implications of this doctrine of sonship of God. [3 marks]

answer: (a) Galatians 3:23-29; 4:1-7: (i) Every man was under the law, kept under restraint until faith was revealed. (ii) The law was our custodian until Christ came, that we might be justified by faith. (iii) Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian (the law). (iv) In Christ Jesus, we are all sons of God through faith. (v) This implies that Christians share sonship of God through Christ who is the Son of God. (vi) He has reconciled us to God through faith. (vii) Through baptism, the believer in Christ has put on Christ, we become one in Christ (Jew or gentile, slave or free, male or female). (viii) Now in Christ, we are Abraham's children, heirs according to promise and not according to the law. (ix) As the young heir remains under guardians and trustees until the date set by his father, so we, as babes, were slaves to the elemental spirits of the world. (x) At the appointed time, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, so that we might receive adoption as sons. (xi) Now that we are adopted as sons, God had sent the spirit of his Son into our hearts, so we bodly call God, 'Father'. (xii) Hence, through. God, Paul explained, we are no longer slaves but sons, and as sons, then heirs. (b) Three implications of the doctrine: (i) The doctrine of sonship implies that the Christian is no longer alien to the household of God, but a bonafide member of the Kingdom of God through Christ. (ii) The Christian shares the blessings of Abraham. (iii) The Son of God had redeemed us and reconciled us to God and had given us the privilege to share with him the right of inheritance of God's eternal glory. (iv) We now have every right to approach the Father, at all times, for whatever need may arise and are assured of his presence and help. (v) With the spirit of his Son in us, we also share Christ's victory. (vi) Christians are no more under the law. (vii) Christians are children of God. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) With reference to first Peter, how should Christian leaders relate to their followers. [9 marks] (b) State any three problems which confront Christian leaders today. [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: With reference to first Peter, how should Christian leaders relate to their followers. [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State any three problems which confront Christian leaders today. [6 marks]

answer: (a) I Peter 5: 1- 4, 6 11: (i) Peter refers to Christian leaders as witnesses of the suffering of Christ and partakers of the glory that is to be revealed during his second coming. (ii) They should, therefore, look after the flock of Christ with tenderness. (iii) They should not regard their assignment as a burden, rather, they should discharge their duties willingly. (iv) Not for shameful material gain but eagerly. (v) Not by being overbearing, but serving as true example/role model to the flock. (vi) They would reap their due reward in due course when the Lord comes. (vii) Leaders should humble themselves under the mighty hand of God for God to exalt them. (viii) They must be sober and watchful because Satan is roaring around looking for whom to destroy. (ix) They should resist Satan at all costs and be firm in their faith. (x) Suffering is part of the Christian life. (xi) God will reward them for their role. (b) Three problems facing Church leaders: (i) Problem of handling the youth. (ii) Rivalry between the youth and elders. (iii) External opposition form Government. (iv) Church finance. (v) Tribalism/nepotism (vi) Status of women/gender issue/gay marriage (vii) Doctrinal issues (viii) Declining faith among followers/backsliding (ix) Greed/materialism (x) Disregard for authority (xi) Position seeking. Previous

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Give account of Joshua's farewell address: [11 marks] (b) Outline two leadership qualities which he manifested during this occasion. [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give account of Joshua's farewell address: [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Outline two leadership qualities which he manifested during this occasion. [4 marks]

answer: a(i) Jos. 24: 1 - 28: (i) Joshua gathered all Israel to Shechem and told the people their history from Abraham to Moses. (ii) He emphasized God's abiding faith with Israel making them owners of the land of the Amorites. (iii) He reminded them of the saving acts of God in their history. (iv) With all these favours, they must serve God and put away all foreign gods. (v) Alternatively, they should decide on whom to serve. (vi) Joshua told the people that as for him and his family, they would serve the Lord. (vii) The Israelites also said they would put away other gods serve the Lord. (viii) Who had been faithful to them. (ix) Joshua reminded them that God is Holy and jealous. (x) He will not forgive their sins/unfaithfulness should they forsake God they would be punished. (xi) He told them not to break their promise. (xii) They must put away all false gods and serve God with sincerity. (xiii) Joshua wrote down the laws of God, put a stone to witness, should they deal falsely with God. (b) Two leadership qualities: (i) He had faith in God. (ii) His ways of life as a role model for his people. (iii) His ability to convince and advise the people to accept his views. (iv) His courage to call the people together. (v) He was a good political leader.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Give an account of the healing of Naaman. [9 marks] (b) What three lessons can be derived from this story? [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give an account of the healing of Naaman. [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: What three lessons can be derived from this story? [6 marks]

answer: (a) 2 Kings 5: 1 — 15: (i) Naaman was the commander of the army of the King of Syria. (ii) He was favoured by the king because through him God had given Syrian victory. (iii) But he was a leper. (vi) During one of their raids, a little maid was captured from Israel. (v) The maid who waited on Naaman's wife and told her mistress that if only his master would visit Israel, his leprosy would be cured. (vi) The wife told her husband what the maid said. (vii) The king of Syria heard of it and gave a letter to Naaman to take to the king of Israel. (viii) Including ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and some festal garments. (ix) When the king of Israel received the letter, he rented his clothes and said am I God that would heal leprosy. (x) The king of Syria was only looking for opportunity to quarrel with him. (xi) When Elisha, the man of God, heard about it he asked Naaman to see him and that he would know that there is a God in Israel. (xii) So, Naaman went to Elisha, the prophet, with his entourage and stood at the gate. (xiii) Elisha sent a message to him that he should go and wash in river Jordan seven times. (xiv) He was angry that there were better rivers in his place than river Jordan. (xv) But his servants urged him and he went and washed in river Jordan seven times. (xvi) And his leprosy left him and his skin was restored. (xvii) He then returned back to Elisha and presented him gifts which Elisha refused. (b) Three lessons derived from the story: (i) Need for humility to achieve success. (ii) We should not visit the house of God with empty hands. (iii) God can use ordinary people (maids) to achieve his purpose. (iv) You don't always need to do extra-ordinary things to get result. (v) Obedience to God's word brings good results. (vi) We should use our gifts/ talents for God. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) How was greed demonstrated in the Life of Gehazi? [12 marks] (b) Give three areas in the society where greed is prevalent. [3 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: How was greed demonstrated in the Life of Gehazi? [12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give three areas in the society where greed is prevalent. [3 marks]

answer: (a) 2Kings 5:16 — 27: (i) After the cleansing of Naaman at River Jordan, he then returned to the man of God with all his company. (ii) He then presented gifts to Elisha the prophet which he refused even after persuasion. (iii) But when Naaman had gone a short distance, Gehazi, Elisha's servant, followed him. (iv) When Naaman saw him, he alighted from his chariot to meet him. (v) He asked if all was well, and Gehazi said that his master sent him to collect the gift. (vi) He then collected the two talents of silver in two bags and some garments. (vii) He put them on two of his servants to carry them for Gehazi. (viii) And when they came close home he collected the items from them and sent the men away. (ix) He then hid them in his room. (x) Later, his master Elisha asked him "where have you been Gehazi?" (xi) He lied that he went nowhere. (xii) His master said he was with him in the spirit and he saw the things he collected from Naaman. (xiii) He, therefore, cursed him that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him and his descendants forever. (xiv) And it was so/He became leprous immediately. (b) Three areas in which greed is prevalent: (i) In the political circle. (ii) In business. (iii) In family. (iv) In the church. (v) In the office. (vi) In sharing things Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Highlight the message of Isaiah to the people of Judah. [11 marks] (b) In what two ways can Christians ensure God's holiness in their country? [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the message of Isaiah to the people of Judah. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what two ways can Christians ensure God's holiness in their country? [4 marks]

answer: (a) Isaiah 1:10-20 (i) Isaiah asked the people of Israel to listen to the word of God. (ii) That their sacrifices were meaningless/God was fed up with their burnt offerings of ram and beast. (iii) God was not delighted in the blood of bulls and lambs. (iv) Because they trampled on justice. (v) Their new moon and Sabbath He hated. (vi) Their offering was vain and incense, an abomination. (vii) So he hid his face from them and would not listen to their prayers. (viii) They should wash and be clean by removing evil from their doing. (ix) They should cease to do evil and learn to do good. (x) They should seek justice and correct oppression. (xi) They should defend the fatherless and plead for the widow. (xii) He told them to come to God and confess their sins so that they could be as white as snow. (xiii) He told them if they were willing and obedient they would eat the good of the land. (xiv) Should they refuse, they would be devoured. (b) Two ways to ensure holiness: (i) By fighting the cause of the poor/ needy. (ii) By asking for forgiveness of sins. (iii) By correcting/mending our ways. (iv) By serving God whole-heartedly. (v) By forsaking sins. (vi) By rebuking/correcting sinners. (vii) By praying consistently. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Narrate the story of the healing of the paralytic. [9 marks] (b) In what three ways is faith relevant to the Christian? [6 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate the story of the healing of the paralytic. [9 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways is faith relevant to the Christian? [6 marks]

answer: (a) Matthew 9:1— 8; Mark 2: 1 — 12; Luke 5:17 26 (i) Jesus came by boat to Capernaum. (ii) The friends of the paralytic brought him to Jesus to be healed. (iii) The whole house was so crowded that they lowered him through the roof. (iv) When Jesus saw their faith, he said. (v) "My son, your sins are forgiven". (vi) The pharisees and Scribes accused Jesus of blasphemy. (vii) Saying only God can forgive sins. (viii) Jesus asked them why they should think evil in their hearts. (ix) "Which is easier, your sins are forgiven or rise and take up your pallet and walk?" (x) That the son of man has authority to forgive sin. (xi) He told the paralytic to rise and take up his bed and go home. (xii) He rose and went home. (xiii) When the crowd saw him, they glorified God. (b) Three ways faith is relevant in the miracle: (i) With faith, healing miracle is possible. (ii) Christ is always ready to help those who have faith in him. (iii) Faith compels people to go to Christ. (iv) Faith in Christ is necessary for all Christians. (vi) Faith in Christ assures Christians of salvation. (vi) Faith makes the impossible, possible/with faith in God, all things are possible. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) "... Who is my neighbours?" How did Jesus answer this question? [12 marks] (b) In what three ways can Christians show good neighbourliness? [3 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: "... Who is my neighbours?" How did Jesus answer this question? [12 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways can Christians show good neighbourliness? [3 marks]

answer: (a) Luke 10:25 — 37 (i) In response to the question posed by a lawyer, "teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" (ii) Jesus said a man was traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho and was attacked by robbers. (iii) They stripped him, beat him and left him and left half-dead. (iv) A priest passed by, saw the wounded man but did not help him. (v) A Levite was also passing by, saw the wounded man and left him. (vi)A certain Samaritan who was on his journey saw the wounded man and had compassion on him. (vii) He went to him and bound his wounds. (viii) He put oil and wine into his wounds and placed him on his horse and carried him to an inn. (ix) Immediately, he made advance payment. (x) He promised to pay any additional bill when he returned. (xi) The man took proper care of the wounded man. (xii) After the story, Jesus asked the lawyer which of the three men was his neighbor? (xiii) The lawyer responded that it was the man who showed mercy. (xiv) Jesus asked him to do likewise. (b) Three ways by which Christians show good neighborliness: (i) By regarding everyone a fellow human being. (ii) By helping those in need. (iii) By not discrimination against others./We should see ourselves as one. (iv) By showing love to one another. (v) By showing good neighbourliness. /Bringing wrongdoing to peoples' attention. (vi) Forgiving those who offend you. (vii) Sharing what you have with others. (viii) Consoling others. / Praying for others. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: (a) Summarize Jesus' teaching about himself as the Resurrection and the Life. [11 marks] (b) Give two assurances Christians have in Christ as the Resurrection and the Life. [4 marks]

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Summarize Jesus' teaching about himself as the Resurrection and the Life. [11 marks]

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give two assurances Christians have in Christ as the Resurrection and the Life. [4 marks]
