The next day, the Philistines settled in the abandoned cities of Israel and sent words of victory over Israel to all their men in Philistine. x. Saul's head was cut off and his armour stripped off as trophies of their victim. xi. These were sent into the temple of Ashtaroth to ascribe the victory to their gods. xii. Saul's body was then fastened to the wall of Bethshan to make fun of him. xiii. However, the people of Jabesh-Gilead went bravely at night to remove Saul and his sons' bodies from Bethshan. xiv. The bodies were brought to Jabesh where they were burnt and the remains buried under the tamarisk tree. xv. This was to avoid further abuse and humiliation/insult on the Israelities. xvi. The people fasted seven days to mourn for Saul and his sons. xvii. They did these things to reciprocate how Saul saved them once when they were threatened by Nahash, the Ammonite King. (B) EFFECTS OF DISOBEDIENCE i. Disobedience breaks up relationships. ii. Disobedience makes us lose favour with God. iii. Disobedience can bring about wars and disasters/death, etc. iv. it creates disunity. v. It tarnishes one's reputation. vi. Disobedience exposes the individual to harm and dangers/it attracts punishment. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline four out of the punishments Amos warned Israel about.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: List three out of the sins Amos condemned which are prevalent today.

answer: (A) PUNISHMENTS AMOS WARNED ISRAEL ABOUT (AMOS 2:6, 4; 5:1-24, 7:10-17,8) i. As Amos identified the transgressions of Israel, God made it clear to them that He would not revoke the punishments if they refused to repent. ii. Amos prophesied that the Samaritan women would be taken to exile in hooks like a fish and cast into Harmon. iii. The women who supported their husbands to oppress the poor would be humiliated and also taken into exile. iv. People who cheated the poor to build hewn stone houses would not dwell in them nor would they live to drink the wine of the vineyards they planted. They would suffer exile as a punishment. v. In all the squares, there shall be wailing, and in all the streets they shall say, Alas! vi. This implies that people would endure bitter punishments leading to wailings here and there. vii. According to Amos, their wives would be harlots in the city, and their sons and daughters would fall by the sword. viii. This implies that a nation would attack and defeat Israel and send them into exile. ix. All businessmen who exploited the poor in the course of their transactions would have their hopes dashed while their feast would turn into mourning. x. Those who looked forward to the day of the Lord as a day of joy and exoneration would be disappointed as it would turn out to be a day of judgment and severe punishment. xi. Worship involving sacrifices, prayers, songs on the feast and sacred days would incur God's displeasure, hatred and rejection. xii. Songs of thanksgiving for harvest would be turned to sadness. xiii. According to Amos, the people would suffer famine not of food or drink but for the word of God. (B) SINS AMOS CONDEMNED WHICH ARE PREVALENT TODAY i. Cult prostitution (Marriage to the gods and priests). ii. Paying lip service to God. iii. Idolatry/false worship/false prophets. iv. Not keeping the Sabbath and feast days holy. v. False swearing/bearing false witnesses. vi. Bribery and corruption. vii. Selling the righteous for money and the needy for a small fee. viii. Cheating in markets with false weights/measures. ix. Forced slavery/child labour/child abuse/child trafficking. x. Sexual immorality, e.g. homosexuality/ fornication/adultery. xi. Luxury as a result of cheating (under/overpayments, fraudulent activities, etc.) xii. Robbing the poor of their properties, e.g. Land guards, etc. xiii. Injustice in the law courts. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate the events that led to the statement "This is my beloved Son with whom I am well pleased."

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Discuss four steps to take to become committed to God.

answer: (A) EVENTS THAT LED TO THE STATEMENT "THIS IS MY BELOVED SON WITH WHOM I AM WELL PLEASED" (MATTHEW 3:13-17, MARK 1:9-11, LUKE 3:21-22.) i. All the synoptic gospels reported the baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist, thus their account were very identical. ii. According to the gospels, Jesus came down from Nazareth of Galilee to be baptized by John the Baptist in the river Jordan. iii. Matthew records the John recognized Jesus as the expected Messiah when he saw Him. iv. He wondered why Jesus should come to him for baptism since Jesus was superior to him. v. John, therefore, became hesitant in baptizing Jesus. vi. However, Jesus persuaded John to baptize him saying, let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness. vii. John then agreed and had Jesus baptized. viii. As Jesus came out of the water, the heavens opened and the Spirit of the Lord descended upon Him like a dove. ix. Then a voice was heard from heaven, saying, "This is my beloved son, with whom I am well pleased." x. The text above alluded to the baptism of Jesus as an event that marked Jesus' call into the ministry. xi. The voice quoted confirmed Jesus as the Messiah/ anointed son/the Christ. xii. Jesus got baptized in order to identify Himself with the sinners He came to redeem. xiii. The Holy Spirit which came upon Jesus led and guided Him to do God's will. xiv. Going to John for baptism was a sign of lending support to John's work. xv. There is disparity among the synoptic gospels about the time the dove descended on Jesus; while Matthew and Mark said that this happened as Jesus was being baptized, Luke said it happened after the baptism. xvi. Similarly, only Matthew reported John's reluctance to baptize Jesus. xvii. Luke reported that after He had been baptized, Jesus prayed and the heavens opened and the Holy Spirit, in the form of a dove, descended upon Him. xviii. The voice from heaven made Jesus conscious of his Messiahship and of His future suffering. xix. The significance of the voice at Jesus' baptism indicates that he had the fullest realization that he was the messiah through suffering, service and obedience to God. xx. By submitting to John's baptism, Jesus gave his approval of John's ministry of baptism and repentance for the forgiveness of sins. (B) STEPS TO TAKE TO BECOME COMMITTED TO GOD i. Obedience to God's commandments/trusting and relying on God. ii. Engaging in church duties and activities, e.g. worship, seminars, crusades, evangelism, etc. iii. Scripture studies and its application to life. iv. Tolerance/respect for other faiths. v. Knowing more about the beliefs and practices of one's religion. vi. Caring for the poor and needy. vii. Seeking forgiveness through confession and forgiving one another. viii. Readiness to accept responsibility. ix. Purity and holiness by living a morally upright life. x. Being prayerful and God-fearing. xi. Loving/respecting one another. xii. Patriotism/concern for one's nation. xiii. Obedience to civil authority/patriotism. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES a) Highlight nine roles played by women in the resurrection stories according to the synoptic gospels. b) Identify three roles played by women in the church today.
answer: A) ROLES WOMEN PLAYED IN THE RESURRECTION STORIES ACCORDING TO THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS (MATTHEW 28:1-10, MARK 16:1-11, LUKE 24:1-11) i . According to the Synoptic gospels, women were the first to go to the tomb of Jesus. ii. Matthew wrote that the women went to the tomb after the Sabbath was fully completed. Mark said it was after the Sabbath had passed and very early in the morning at the rising of the sun. iii. The women were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Salome. Luke added Joana, the wife of Chuza. iv. According to Mark, these four women brought sweet spices to anoint the body of Jesus for further embalming. v. While on their way, the women wondered who would help them roll away the rock at the entrance of the tomb. vi. Mathew, however, reported that there was a great earthquake before the women got there. vii. An angel of the Lord from heaven rolled back the stone and sat upon it. viii. For fear of the angel, the guards were frightened and became like dead men. ix. The angel told the women not to be afraid, for Jesus had risen and they should come and see where he was laid. x. The angel told them to go quickly and tell the disciples that he had arisen and was going to Galilee where they would meet him. xi. Matthew did not say that the angel appeared to the women but only to the guards. xii. According to Mark, when the women entered the tomb, they saw a young man sitting at the right side, in a white robe and when they went in, they did not find the body of Jesus; thus, they were perplexed. xiii. The women then saw the vision of the angel who gave them information regarding the resurrection of Christ. xiv. They were asked to inform the disciples. Mark made emphasis to Peter. xv. The women left quickly from the tomb with awe and ran to tell the disciples that Jesus had arisen. xvi. But before then, Jesus had appeared to them, saluting them, 'Hail' as they took hold of his feet and worshipped him. (B) ROLES OF WOMEN IN THE CHURCH TODAY i. Some women study hard and with faith, they become Pastors, Rev. Sisters, and Prophetesses/ some women are powerful prayer warriors. ii. Others also help as lay readers and Catechists/ Ushers/ Evangelists/ Preachers. iii. They help in the liturgy by joining the choir to sing in the church. iv. Some give out their properties (like houses) for the use of the church, e.g. cell/home fellowship meetings, leaders meetings, etc. v. Others adopt and raise Priests out of their bounty/ become benefactors. vi. Most of the cleaning activities to keep the church tidy and other church decorations are spearheaded by women. vii. Women also play major roles in the running of orphanages, crèches, schools and vocational institutions of churches. viii. Charity works of the church like distribution of aids and catering for the poor, sick and the marginalised are mostly done by women/ distribution of communion elements. ix. Several women societies are formed to help or support the running of the church, e.g. Women's Fellowship, Christian Mothers, etc. x. Organising seminars/workshops/ counselling sessions. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLE

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Narrate Peter's miraculous escape from prison.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three factors that motivate people to pray.

answer: (A) PETER'S MIRACULOUS ESCAPE FROM PRISON (ACTS 12:1-19) i. Herod Agrippa opposed and persecuted the church. ii. He killed James, the brother of John. iii. When Herod realised that the death of James pleased the Jews, he went ahead to arrest Peter. iv. This arrest took place during the celebration of the feast of the unleavened bread. v. Herod intended to have Peter killed after the Passover celebrations. vi. The night before the day Herod planned to kill Peter, Peter was bound with chains and placed between two soldiers/ he was heavily guarded to prevent his escape. vii. While Peter was in prison, constant prayers were said on his behalf. viii. As Peter was asleep, an angel of the Lord appeared to him and a light shone in the cell. ix. The angel touched and woke him up, saying, "Get up quickly." x. Immediately, the chains fell off from his hands and the angel told him to dress up Which Peter obeyed. xi. The angel then commanded Peter to follow him. xii. Peter thought that he was dreaming all the while. xiii. But when he passed through the first and second gates and came to the Iron Gate leading into the city, the gate opened of its own accord. xiv. When the angel left Peter, he realised that the Lord had sent an angel to rescue him from the power of Herod. xv. Peter immediately went to the house of Mary the mother of John Mark where the brethren had gathered to pray for him in the middle of the night. xvi. When Peter knocked at the door, Rhoda identified his voice and told the brethren that Peter was at the door knocking. xvii. But the brethren expressed disbelief and said Rhoda was mad. xviii. They said the one at the door might be Peter's angel/ghost. xix. Eventually, when the door was opened and they saw Peter, they were amazed and wanted to shout for joy but Peter restrained them. xx. Peter described how his release from prison happened and he later fled from Jerusalem. xxi. As Peter could not be found in the morning after a search, Herod ordered for the execution of the guards. (B) FACTORS THAT MOTIVATE PEOPLE TO PRAY i. In times of sickness/stress or difficult, etc. (Petition/Supplication Prayer). ii. When people sin against God, they pray to confess their sins and ask for forgiveness (Confessional prayer). iii. To dedicate or commit oneself to God as a new being (Dedication prayer). iv. To bless or consecrate an object/building, vestment, etc. v. To seek God's counsel or favours in making important decisions, e.g. examinations, interviews, etc. vi. To obtain protection against evil/the devil. vii. The desire for spiritual growth. viii. To intercede for loved ones going through affliction (Intercessory prayers). ix. For adoration/appreciation or thanksgiving to God for His mercies (Thanksgiving prayer). x. When led by the Holy Spirit/fellowship of believers. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline James' argument on faith without works is dead.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Indicate three benefits of faith to a Christian.

answer: (A) JAMES' ARGUMENT ON FAITH WITHOUT WORKS IS DEAD (JAMES 1:22-27; 2:14-26) i. James advised Christians to live according to the word of the Lord which they had heard. ii. He said it would be no use to hear the word and fail to put it into practice. iii. According to James, if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like someone who sees himself in a mirror and turns away and immediately forgets himself. iv. James points out that he who observes the perfect law of liberty and perseveres in it by acting and not only being a hearer would be blessed in his doing. v. According to James, God's blessing comes through works and not faith. vi. James was of the opinion that if one thinks he is religious but does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is vain. vii. He held the view that practical and unidentified religion before God entails the visitation of orphans and widows in their affliction. viii. And also keeping oneself unstained from the world. ix. James said it is of no use to say you have faith but have no works to demonstrate the faith you have. x. He taught that faith must be combined with practical works to produce the desired results. xi. According to James, if someone was poorly clothed and hungry and you asked him to go in peace and be filled without providing the clothes and food for them, you are not backing your faith with works. xii. Hence, faith without works is dead and useless. xiii. He asserted that it is not enough to believe in God. xiv. Belief in the only true. God is good, for even the devil also believes in God, but does not do the will of Him. Hence, faith in God without works is unacceptable. xv. James cited two Old Testament figures who exhibited faith and works in unison. For example, Abraham justified his faith by works when he was prepared to sacrifice his son Isaac. xvi. According to James, faith is justified by works; hence, Abraham believed in God and it was counted to him as righteousness and he was called a friend of God because he acted on his faith. xvii. A person is therefore justified by works and not by faith alone. xviii. Similarly, Rahab, the prostitute justified her faith by works when she received the messengers of Joshua and sent them out by another way. xix. James concluded by saying that as the body without the spirit is dead so also faith without works is dead. xx. Faith should manifest itself in the love of God and service to humankind and not the mere expression of it by words alone. (B) BENEFITS OF FAITH TO A CHRISTIAN i. Faith helps Christians to believe and trust God/have fellowship with Him. ii. It enables Christians to be committed to God/depend and rely on Him. iii. It assures Christians of eternal salvation. iv. It shows that Christians are not under law but under grace. v. It is by faith that Christians face life's challenges with courage and strength, e.g. persecution. vi. Faith motivates Christians to do good works in all fields, e.g. Education, Medicare, Evangelism, caring for the poor and the needy. vii. It enables believers to have hope/grow spiritually/keep God's commandments. viii. It promotes healing/it is a factor in receiving miracles. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give twelve reasons why Christians should remain loyal to their masters in all situations.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Identify any three virtues worthy of practice by Christians.

answer: (A) REASONS WHY CHRISTIANS SHOULD REMAIN LOYAL TO THEIR MASTERS IN ALL SITUATIONS — (1 PETER 2:18-25) i. Christians should be law-abiding and have respect for constituted authorities. ii. Christians should discharge their civic duties and responsibilities promptly to all men/masters even if they were gentle or harsh towards them. iii. Peter taught that a good Christian should submit himself and respect every human institution, including the authorities of the state, e.g. Governors, etc. iv. For it is God who appointed kings to punish wrongdoers and to reward those who do good. v. He stressed that the Christians' good behaviour would put to shame the ignorance of foolish men. vi. As men who have been liberated from the curse of the law, a good Christian citizen should live as a freeman without using his freedom as a pretext for evil. vii. But rather, he should live as an obedient servant of God. viii. Besides, he should respect every man and love the brotherhood of believers. ix. Furthermore, he should fear God and honour the king and rulers. x. Peter cited the case of the unjust suffering of Christ as an example worthy of emulation / He was sinless yet without retaliation x. Jesus did not threaten his persecutors but trusted in God who would give the right judgment at the end. xii. Jesus died for our sins and by His wounds, we are healed. xiii. According to James, we were straying like sheep but Jesus our shepherd showed us the way. xiv. Christian servants should therefore follow the good example of Jesus in all things. (B) VIRTUES WORTHY OF PRACTICE BY CHRISTIANS i. Patience. ii. Obedience. iii. Endurance. iv. Love/Kindness. v. Faithfulness. vi. Respect/Fear of God. vii. Perseverance. viii. Forgiveness ix. Honesty/Sincerity/Integrity/Truthfulness. x. Patriotism/Loyalty. xi. Humility. xii. Righteousness/Holiness/Purity. xiii. Pervert/Persistent prayer. xiv. Chastity. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT CIRCUMSTANCES UNDER WHICH JOSEPH WAS SET FREE FROM PRISON (GENESIS 41:1-44).
answer: Below are the expected points candidates should construct their points from: i. After his encounter with Potiphar’s wife, Joseph was imprisoned. ii. While in prison, Joseph interpreted the dreams of the chief butler and the chief baker of the king of Egypt. iii. Two years later Pharaoh had two dreams. iv. In the first dream Pharaoh saw seven giant and thin cows. v. And to his surprise, the thin ones swallowed the fat ones. vi. In the second dream seven thin ears of grain swallowed seven plump ears of grain. vii. Pharaoh was disturbed because none of his magicians and wise men could interpret the dreams. viii. It was at this time that the King’s chief butler remembered who interpreted his dream in prison. ix. The butler then told Pharaoh of Joseph’s ability to interpret his dream. x. Pharaoh instantly requested that Joseph be brought out of the prison. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: WHY REHOBOAM WAS UNABLE TO PRESERVE HIS ROYAL LINEAGE (1 KINGS 12: 1-20).
answer: Only a few candidates were able to trace the causes of the fall of the kingdom which are being highlighted below; After the death of Solomon, his son Rehoboam was made the King of Judah. He went to Schechem to be installed as king. However, when Jeroboam heard about this, he returned from exile in Egypt to lead a delegation from the North to Rehoboam. They said; “your father made our yoke heavy, lighten the hard service of your father and we will serve you”. Rehoboam asked them to go and come back in three days’ time. He wisely took the first step to consult with his royal advisers who had served his father Solomon. He was advised to listen to the plea of the Northerners and they would be his servants forever. But he accepted the advice of his contemporaries and ignored that of the elders. He promised to add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpion.i.e. increase their burden. Armed with the advice of the contemporaries, he announced the outright rejection of the request of the people. He promised them a harder regime than his father’s. Rehoboam’s response was to bring to pass the prophecy of Ahijah, concerning the division of the kingdom. When the people realized that the king did not listen to their request, they withdrew their union with the southern tribes. Hence the statement: “what portion do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, O Israel”! Rehoboam was therefore advised to go back to Judah and take care of his people. Israel departed to their tent and Jeroboam was installed as King of the North. Point expected of candidates in the B part includes; We should learn to respect popular opinion. We should be diplomatic, tactical and sensible in handling crisis. The best method through which conflict can be resolved is dialogue. High- handedness is capable of aggravating or fuelling crises. We should be aware of negative peer-group influence. We should learn to imbibe the rudiments of democracy. Parents should live good lifestyles for their children to emulate. The words of elders are often words of wisdom and should be listened to. We should be sensitive to our ethical/religious sentiments. We should avoid making unwise decisions. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: HOW MESHACH, SHADRACH AND ABEDNEGO DEMONSTRATED THEIR FAITH IN GOD (DANIEL 3: 1-30).
answer: Candidates are expected to highlight some of the essential points as listed below; Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were devout Jews brought into captivity in Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar. They were dedicated to the worship of their God and rigid observance of the Israelite laws. Owing to their outstanding qualities, the King appointed the three men to high positions of authority in the country. Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon set up a golden image to be worshipped by all his subjects and nations under him. All officials of his Kingdom were assembled for the dedication of the golden image. Nebuchadnezzar’s official proclamation was backed up by a decree in case of any violation. Whoever defied the King’s order of worshipping the golden image was to be cast into a burning fiery furnace. The Chaldeans conspired against Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. They were accused of disobeying the King’s order of worshipping the golden image. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were summoned by Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar gave the three another opportunity to worship the golden image. They rejected the offer to worship the golden image saying, “be it known to you, O king that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have setup”. Nebuchadnezzar became furious at their refusal He ordered that they be cast into the burning fiery furnace. (B) LESSONS THAT CAN BE LEARNT FROM THE INCIDENT IN (A) ABOVE The incident offers hope to believers who suffer as a result of persecution/ opposition. It is a special source of encouragement to believers. It shows that judgment is certain and God’s servants will be vindicated. It can sustain believers going through persecution. It teaches that the world may seem out of control but God reigns. God cares for believers who take a stand for Him. Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego demonstrated incredible courage which believers should emulate. It reveals an in-depth knowledge of the supremacy of the Almighty God. It helps to strengthen believers’ faith in God/ confidence in God. God’s enemies shall never go unpunished. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: CONTRIBUTIONS OF CYRUS TO THE REBUILDING OF THE TEMPLE IN JERUSALEM (EZRA 1:1-11).
answer: The points candidates are expected to develop are: Cyrus was the king of Persia who captured Babylon. During the first year of his reign, God inspired him to promulgate a decree in fulfilment of Jeremiah’s prophecy. In the decree, he said God had given him all the kingdoms of the earth. And that God has charged him to build a house at Jerusalem for Him. Immediately, he ordered the Jews to return to Jerusalem to build the house of the God of Israel. Heads of the father’s houses of Judah and Benjamin rose up to go. The Priests and the Levites were also inspired to go. Cyrus returned the vessels of gold and silver which Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and placed them in the house of his gods. They were handed over to Sheshebazzar, the prince of Judah to be returned to Jerusalem. Cyrus further stated that every exile was to be helped by his neighbour or men of his place with silver and gold and animals. Freewill offerings were to be included as contributions towards the rebuilding projects. He also helped financially towards the rebuilding programme. King Cyrus fulfilled the dreams of the exiles who for that matter viewed him as the Lord’s anointed or as an instrument of God to free the Jews. In the B part, the points expected of candidates include; It is our civic responsibility. It is our contribution to socio-economic development. There is pride/dignity. We feel part of the development process/sense of belonging. We can proudly protect what we have. It keeps us active. It strengthens co-operation and unity. It is a call to show/demonstrate patriotism. It is a divine command. It enables us to leave a legacy of posterity. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: JESUS’ ENCOUNTER WITH MATHEW, THE TAX COLLECTOR (MARK 2:13-17, MATTHEW 9:9-13, LUKE 5:27-32).
answer: Points expected of candidates are highlighted below: As Jesus passed by, he saw Mathew sitting at the tax office in Capernaum. Jesus called him saying “follow me”. And he rose and followed him. Mark called this tax collector Levi, the son of Alphaeus. Later, Mathew organized a feast in his house for Jesus and His disciples. Many tax collectors came to sit at the table with Jesus and His disciples. As they dined, the Scribes and the Pharisees murmured: and criticised Jesus saying“why does he eat with tax-collectors and sinners”? When Jesus heard it, he said to them: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.” “I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” He asked them to go and learn the meaning of the following statement: “I desire mercy and not sacrifice” In the B part, candidates are to list out points that can be leant from the encounter between Jesus and Matthew. Some of which include: Religious/ Vocational calls are mandatory- they need to be obeyed. God can use anyone to fulfil His purpose. Discrimination/ distinctions should be avoided/Need to respect and treat people equally. No profession is more important than the other/We should not look down on some professions. God hates sin but loves the sinner. One good turn deserves another/ need to reciprocate good gestures/ show gratitude. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
answer: Candidates are expected to understand the activities that led to the denial as outlined below; After the last supper, Jesus and His disciples left for Mount Olivet. On the way, Jesus prophesied that the disciples would soon flee away from Him. This was to fulfil a scripture which said “I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered. Jesus added that he would go ahead to Galilee after His resurrection. Peter cut in that he would not desert Jesus even if the others did. Jesus then predicted that Peter would deny Him three times before the cock would crow twice that night. True to Jesus’ prediction, the disciples except Peter fled away when Jesus was arrested in Gethsemane. Luke, however, said Jesus’ prediction of the denial came when Peter claimed dying or being imprisoned for Jesus’ sake. Those who arrested Jesus took Him to Caiaphas’ house while Peter followed at a distance. Peter mingled with some of the guards who were warming themselves in the courtyard. After a while, a maid of the high priest while passing by identified Peter as one of the followers of Jesus the Nazarene. Peter denied this saying “I neither know nor understand what you mean”. Peter then moved to the gateway, where another man next to him told the bystanders that Peter was with Jesus. Peter quickly denied for the second time that he didn’t even know Jesus. After a while, the bystanders confronted Peter that he was a disciple of Jesus for his accent revealed him as a Galilean. Peter became angry invoking curses and swearing for not knowing Jesus. Immediately, the cock crowed twice when he denied Jesus the third time. Peter then recalled Jesus’ prediction that before the cock crowed twice he would have denied Him three times. Peter left the place as he broke down and wept bitterly. Points expected of candidates in the B part are outlined below; Lack of parental care/love/affection. Wickedness/maltreatment/ insults of parents. Unfaithfulness in marital issues. Neglect/denial of basic needs. Sacrilege/Incest/Grievous sins e.g. murder, seizure of properties. Refusal to parent a child/ disowning of pregnancies. Treachery/cheating/deceits/betrayals. Breaking of covenants/Vows/Secret revelations. Some parents mistreat their spouses and their children become bitter against them, hence renouncing them as parents later on. Some parents who travel outside the country refuse to care for their spouse and children. When one spouse toils to care for the children, the children grow to hate the other parent. Some parents become alcoholic and their children become ashamed to call them their parents before their friends. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: MAIN FEATURES OF COMMUNAL LIFE OF THE EARLY CHURCH (ACTS 2:41-47, 4:32-37)
answer: Points candidates need to include in the A part are; Following Peter’s speech at Pentecost, three thousand (3000) people were added to the church. The new converts were then baptised. Believers engaged in fellowship/ breaking of bread/prayers. Many signs and wonders were performed by the apostles. All the believers shared their possessions. The people praised God. God kept bringing people into the church. Food was eaten with happiness. Believers were with the oneness of heart/ soul. No one said that any of the things which he possessed was his own. They all had everything in common. The apostles testified to the resurrection of Jesus Christ. There was not a needy person among the believers. Some land/ house owners sold their properties and brought the money for the upkeep of the people. E.g Barnabas. Distribution was made to each as any had need. However, Ananias and Sapphira his wife were not sincere in giving out their possession and were instantly punished. Another important event which nearly marred/ destroyed the unity of the church was the unfair distribution of provisions. However, this was resolved by the appointment of the deacons. CAUSES OF THE GRADUAL DESTRUCTION OF OUR COMMUNAL VALUES The incursion of Western culture. Greed/Selfishness. Lack of love for others. High level of poverty. People are no longer their brother’s keepers. Lack of commitment by leaders. Lack of parental responsibilities. Urbanization/Modernization. The negative influence of the media. Western Education. Western Religion. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: JAMES’ TEACHING ON THE NEED TO TREAT PEOPLE EQUALLY (JAMES 2:1-13)
answer: Candidates are expected to list out points such as; James in his epistle admonished Christians to be impartial since they profess the faith of Jesus Christ. This is because Jesus Himself does not show partiality. James gave an illustration of a rich man nicely dressed and a poor man shabbily dressed both visiting a church. And it happens that much attention is given to the rich man. The well -dressed rich man is given a special place to sit. But the poorly dressed man is asked to stand at an ordinary place. According to James, in such a situation, discrimination has been made between the rich and the poor. And this makes people become judges with evil thoughts. James says that God has chosen those who are poor materially in this world to be spiritually rich in faith. James holds the view that the poor are the heirs of the kingdom which is promised to those who love God. James further reminded the believers about how the rich dishonour the poor. He said the rich consistently oppress the poor and drag them to court. The rich also blaspheme the honourable name of Jesus. James admonished believers to observe the royal law which is “love your neighbour as yourself”. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: PETER’S TEACHING ON INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIP ON HOW CHRISTIAN ELDERS SHOULD RELATE TO THEIR FOLLOWERS (1 PETER 5:1-11)
answer: Candidates are required to state that; Peter refers to Christian leaders as witnesses of the suffering of Christ and partakers of the glory that is to be revealed during his second coming. They should therefore look after the flock of Christ with tenderness. They should not regard their assignment as a burden rather they should discharge their duties willingly. Not for shameful material gain but eagerly. Not by being overbearing but serving as true examples/role model to the flock. They would reap their due reward in due course when the Lord comes. Leaders should humble themselves under the mighty hand of God for God to exalt them. They must be sober and watchful because Satan is roaming around looking for whom to destroy. They should resist Satan at all costs and be firm in their faith. Suffering is part of the Christian life. God will reward them for their role. Love the brotherhood. Keep a clear conscience so that they can put to shame those who abuse them. He also admonished the younger ones in the church to be subject to the elders. According to Peter, Christians should clothe themselves with humility towards one another. Peter also advised Christians to resist the devil and he would flee from them/ they could resist the devil with their faith in Christ. Finally, they should stand firm in their faith, for the enemy was always seeking an opportunity to attack. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT Relate to how marriage was instituted by God in the second creation story.
answer: Below are the expected points from candidates; 1. In the second creation story, God created man out of dust and gave him breath to become a living being. 2. God placed man in the garden of Eden to keep and till it. 3. So He created all living creatures and charged man to name them but none was fit as a partner for him. 4. God saw that man was lonely. 5. God, therefore, said that it was not good for man to be alone. 6. Hence He decided to make a helper fit for man as his partner. 7. God caused a deep sleep to fall upon man. 8. And while the man slept, He took one of his ribs and closed up its place with flesh. 9. And out of the rib God took from man, He made a woman and brought her to the man. 10. When the man saw the woman, he said, “This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh...”. 11. Man said, she shall be called woman because she was taken out of man. 12. That day, man and woman became married couple. 13. Hence a man leaves his father and mother and cleaves to his wife and they become one flesh. 14. And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT Recount the effects of the behaviour of Eli’s children on Israel as a nation (1 Samuel 2:12-36, 3:2-18, 4:10-22).
answer: Expected answers are highlighted below on the consequences of the behaviours of Eli’s children on Israel; 1. God sent the Philistines to fight Israel. 2. Israel was defeated though she went to war with the ark of God. 3. About three thousand Israelites died in the war. 4. The ark of the covenant was also captured by the Philistines. 5. The two sons of Eli were also killed. 6. Eli died when he heard that his two sons were dead and the ark also captured. 7. When Phinehas’ wife, who was pregnant heard of the death of her husband and the father-in-law, she gave birth prematurely and later died. 8. The child that was born was called Ichabod, meaning, “The glory has departed from Israel.” 9. Thus the priestly position of Eli was taken away from the family. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the religious tension in Israel during the reign of King Ahab

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Identify three steps that can be taken to minimize religious tension in the society.

answer: (A) Religious tension in Israel during the reign of King Ahab. (I kings 16:29-34, 17:1-7, 18: 1-19) In regards to this question, candidates are expected to highlight the points as listed below; 1. Ahab married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, King of the Sidonians. 2. She was a staunch worshipper of Baal of Phoenicia. 3. Jezebel was allowed by Ahab to bring into Israel the worship of Baal together with several Baal prophets and Prophets of Asherah. 4. She tried making Baalism state religion of Israel. 5. In pursuance of her policy, she killed the prophets of God who opposed her. 6. The prophets of God who could not withstand Jezebel fled the country while others were hidden by Obadiah. 7. The altars of Yahweh were also cut down. 8. Ahab helped in the promotion of Baalism as he used state resources to build temples for Baal. 9. Ahab perpetrated grave social injustices during his reign eg. He had Naboth killed and took over his vineyard. 10. Many Israelites deserted Yahweh to worship Baal. 11. All these acts of idolatry and injustice incurred the displeasure of God. 12. It was around this time that Elijah from Tishbe, the prophet of God emerged to confront Ahab. 13. God asked Elijah to pronounce drought in Israel for three and a half years. 14. And as a result of the drought, there was severe famine on the land of Israel. 15. God used ravens to feed Elijah who went to hide by the brook Cherith from where he had water to drink. 16. For a while, Elijah was afraid to meet King Ahab for fear that Jezebel might kill him because she had earlier persecuted the prophets of Yahweh. 17. But after a while, the Lord told Elijah to present himself to King Ahab. 18. Ahab accused Elijah of being the troubler of Israel. 19. But Elijah maintained that it was Ahab and his royal house that had brought the drought because of their worship of Baal. 20. However, the tension was resolved by the contest on Mount Carmel, requested by Elijah. 21. The supremacy of God was established after Elijah won the contest. 22. Elijah then had the Baal prophets killed to reflect his victory over the Baal prophets. (B) Steps that can be taken to minimize religious tensions in society. 1. Tolerance/respect for the views of other religions/ avoid partiality/show love for all religions. 2. Have understanding and concern for others/ avoid derogatory remarks. 3. There should be inter-religious dialogue. 4. The state should recognize all religious faiths/freedom of worship. 5. Desist from greed and covetousness. 6. Do not tolerate evil counsel. 7. Focus on God only/fear God. 8. Sinners must be condemned. 9. Counselling people who go astray. 10. Men of God should speak against injustice/corruption, etc. 11. Using social media to expose evil deeds and doers in society. 12. Rights of citizens should be respected. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: How was greed demonstrated in the life of Gehazi?

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: Give three areas in the society where greed is prevalent.

answer: (A) How greed was demonstrated in the life of Gehazi. (2 Kings 5:14-27) The points expected of candidates are; 1. After the cleansing of Naaman’s leprosy at river Jordan, he returned to the man of God (Elisha) with large amount of gifts. 2. He presented the gifts to Elisha the prophet, but he refused to accept them and dispatched him even after persuasion. 3. When Naaman had gone a short distance with his gifts, Gehazi, Elisha’s servant, followed him to request for the items his master had rejected. 4. Naaman saw him and alighted from his chariot to meet him. 5. He asked if all was well; Gehazi lied, saying that his master had sent him to collect the gifts. 6. Naaman gave Gehazi twice his request and ordered his servants to assist him to carry the items home. 7. He put them on two of his servants to carry them for Gehazi. 8. When they came close home he collected the items from them and sent the men away. 9. He then hid them in his room. 10. Later, his master Elisha got to know the misdeed of his servant and questioned him, ‘Where have you been, Gehazi?” 11. Gehazi lied that he went nowhere. 12. His master said he was with him in spirit and he saw the things he collected from Naaman. 13. He, therefore, cursed him that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him, and his descendants forever. 14. And it was so/ he became leprous immediately, as a result of his greed. In the B part, points expected of candidates include; 1. In the political circle - e.g. Legislative/Judiciary/Executive circles. 2. In business - e.g. profiteering/cheating. 3. In the family/neighbourhood – e.g. land and family properties. 4. Religious institutions/organizations -e.g. Diversion of resources. 5. In the office – Ministries/Departments/Agencies e.g. Bribery and corruption. 6. In the sharing of things/inheritance. 7. Port and harbours/Customs- e.g. clearing of goods/over and under-invoicing. 8. Educational institutions e.g. Examination malpractices/corruption. 9. Police/Immigration - e.g. extortion. 10. Social organisations —NGOs e.g. Corruption, etc. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?” Recount Jesus’ response to the above question.

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: State three lessons that can be learnt from Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness.

answer: (A) Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness (Matthew 18:21-35) Points expected of candidates are highlighted below; 1. Jesus told the story of the unmerciful servant in response to Peter’s question on how often one should show forgiveness to his/her neighbour. 2. Peter asked Jesus if it was seven times one should forgive one’s brother. 3. Jesus told him that one should forgive seventy times seven and not seven times. 4. To illustrate this, Jesus compared the Kingdom of heaven to a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants. 5. In the process, one of his debtors who owed him ten thousand talents was brought to him to settle his debt. 6. As he could not pay his debt, the king ordered that he, his wife, children and all that he had be sold to settle the debt. 7. The debtor then fell on his knees and pleaded with the king to be patient so that he would settle the debt later. 8. Out of pity, the king released the man and forgave him the debt. 9. Interestingly, the same man who was forgiven his debt went out and found his fellow servant who owed him only a hundred denarii. 10. He grabbed him by his throat and demanded instant payment. 11. His fellow servant fell on his knees and pleaded for payment to be made later. 12. But the man refused the request and put his fellow servant in prison until the debt was settled. 13. When his fellow servants saw’ what had happened, they became distressed and reported the case to the king. 14. The king summoned the man and rebuked him for not showing mercy to the fellow servant who owed him. 15. In anger, the King handed the man over to the jailers until he had settled all his debt. 16. Jesus concluded that it is the same way that God would do to every one of us if we do not forgive our brother from our hearts/God would not forgive anyone who failed to forgive others. (B) State three lessons that can be learnt from Jesus’ teaching on forgiveness. 1. It builds trust and confidence among people. 2. It is a sign of maturity. 3. It elicits repentance/remorsefulness and confession. 4. It leads to rehabilitation and reconciliation. 5. Facilitates prayers. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: Examine the trials of Jesus before Pilate as recorded in Luke’s Gospel.

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: State three elements of a fair trial.

answer: (A) The trial of Jesus before Pilate as recorded by Luke’s gospel (Luke 23:1-12) 1. After Jesus had been found guilty of blasphemy for claiming to be the Christ a King, the Jewish Council brought him before Pilate. 2. The Sanhedrin had earlier passed the death sentence on him. 3. But the council had no legal right to execute the death sentence on Jesus without approval from the Romans. 4. The Sanhedrin was therefore required to send Jesus to Pontius Pilate, the Roman representative for trial. 5. And in order to make Jesus guilty before Pilate, they changed the charges levelled against him from religious blasphemy to political insurgence and revolution. 6. Jesus was accused of perverting the nation. 7. He was also charged with claiming to be a king. 8. Jesus was accused of forbidding the payment of taxes to Caesar. 9. Pilate asked Jesus if he was a King of the Jews, and Jesus answered in the affirmative. 10. Eventually, Pilate told the chief Priest and the crowd that Jesus was innocent by saying” I find no crime in this man”. 11. But the people said Jesus stirs up people, teaching throughout all Judea from Galilee. 12. When Pilate discovered that Jesus was a Galilean and belonged to Herod Antipas’ jurisdiction, he decided to send him to Herod Antipas. 13. After Herod had asked Jesus some questions at length and he did not answer, he mocked him and treated him with contempt. 14. Herod realised that Jesus was innocent even though his opponents accused him vehemently. 15. Finally, Herod returned Jesus to Pilate and on that day Pilate and Herod became friends as they were previously enemies. (B) Points expected of candidates are outlined below; 1. People should be given the right to public hearing. 2. People accused must have the right to counsel. 3. Judges in the courts must be impartial and not affected by conflict of interest. 4. People must have the right to appeal or a review of sentence. 5. People must have the right to be heard within a reasonable time. 6. An accused person should be deemed innocent until proven guilty. 7. Evidence should be sufficient and reliable/ no false witnesses. 8. There should be no interference in the work of the Judiciary/ independence of the Judiciary must be respected. 9. Judges must enjoy good conditions of service/ good pay /retire on their salary. 10. The Judiciary should be bold and fearless. 11. Citizens should ensure that justice is done at all times without fear or favour, to all manner of people. 12. Suspects should not be intimidated or tortured to elicit information. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION B: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: Highlight the persecution Peter and John had after the healing of the lame man.

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: Mention two lessons that can be learnt from the reaction of Peter and John.

answer: (A) The persecution of Peter and John after the healing of the lame man. (Acts 4: 1-31) 1. After the healing of the cripple at the Beautiful Gate, the lame man demonstrated his cure by leaping and praising God, as he accompanied the disciples into the temple. 2. Many people recognized the cured man and they were amazed. 3. As they gathered, Peter and John preached and about 5,000 were converted. 4. Peter attributed their ability to heal the man at the Beautiful Gate to the resurrected Christ. 5. There was so much noise in the temple that Peter and John were arrested by the Priests, the Sadducees and the captain of the temple. 6. They were put in custody and tried by the council the following day. 7. During the trial, they were asked to tell the source of the power they used to heal the cripple. 8. Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit answered that it was through the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom they crucified but God raised from the dead. 9. Peter also said that apart from Jesus, there was no other name by which men would be saved. 10. Peter added that Jesus is the stone which the builders rejected but has become the cornerstone. 11. The Sanhedrin upon seeing the boldness of Peter and John and perceiving that they were uneducated, common men, realized that they had been with Jesus. 12. The Council saw the man who had been healed standing with them and they could not press any charge against them. 13. The captain of the temple and the Sadducees who did not believe in the resurrection were annoyed because the disciples were proclaiming Jesus’ resurrection from death. 14. Thus the Sanhedrin decided to restrain Peter and John by commanding them not to speak in the name of Jesus again. 15. But Peter and John resolutely insisted that they would obey God rather than man. 16. They were then set free and they joined the other apostles to pray, thanking God and asking for more boldness to speak the word of God and perform miracles. 17. As they prayed, the place where they stood shook and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. (B) Lessons that can be learnt from the reaction of Peter and John 1. We should be bold and resolute in doing God’s work/perseverance. 2. It is better to obey God than men/have faith in God. 3. Opposition and persecution can never stop God’s work. 4. It is only God who equips one for his work. 5. We should be willing to die for our beliefs. 6. We should pray and thank God in every situation. 7. We need to value our principles. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

subQuestions.label: A
subQuestions.text: Explain James’ advice to Christians to be doers of the word and not hearers only.

subQuestions.label: B
subQuestions.text: State two factors that hinder Christians from doing the will of God.

answer: (A) James’ advice to Christians to be doers of the word and not hearers only. (James 1:22-27, 2:14-26). Candidates are expected to list out points such as; 1. James advised Christians to live according to the word of the Lord, which they have heard. 2. He said it would be of no use to hear the word and fail to put it into practice. 3. According to James, if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer he is like someone who sees himself in a mirror and turns away and immediately forgets. 4. James says that, he who looks into the perfect law, and perseveres by doing it shall be blessed. 5. James is of the opinion that if one thinks he is religious but does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is vain. 6. James holds the view that pure and undefiled religion before God entails visiting orphans and widows in their afflictions. 7. Pure religion also involves keeping oneself unstained from the world. 8. James says it is of no use to say you have faith but have no works to demonstrate the faith you have. 9. According to James, if someone is poorly clothed and hungry and you ask him to go in peace, and be warmed and filled without providing the clothing and food, then you are not backing your faith with works. 10. Hence, faith without works is dead/useless. 11. Abraham justified his faith by works when he was prepared to sacrifice his son, Isaac. 12. Abraham believed God and it was counted as righteousness and he was called a friend of God. 13. A person is therefore justified by works and not faith alone. 14. Similarly, Rahab the prostitute justified her faith by works when she received the messengers of Joshua and sent them out by another way.. 15. James concludes by saying that, as the body without the spirit is dead so also faith without works is dead. (B) Factors that hinder Christians from doing the will of God 1. Lack of faith/backsliding/unforgiving spirit 2. Unpleasant experiences 3. Desire to please the world/Materialism 4. Poverty 5. Fear 6. Lack of commitment/being ashamed to preach the word of God Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES Peter’s teaching on interpersonal relationship among Christians. (1 Peter 5:1-11)
answer: Candidates are required to state that; 1. Peter exhorts elders of the church to tend the flock willingly and not by constraint. 2. The elders are to care for the flock, not for any gain but eagerly. 3. They are not to be domineering over those in their charge. 4. Instead, they are to set good examples for the flock to emulate. 5. Peter made the elders aware that when the chief shepherd appears, they will obtain the unfading crown of glory. 6. Peter also admonished the younger ones in the church to be subject to the elders. 7. According to Peter, Christians should clothe themselves with humility towards one another. 8. As God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble. 9. Peter further advised the younger ones to humble themselves under God’s mighty hand. 10. And in due time, the Lord will exalt them. 11. Peter also advised Christians to cast all their anxieties on the Lord. 12. He asked Christians to resist the devil and he would flee from them. 13. Finally, they should stand firm in their faith for the enemy was always seeking an opportunity to attack them. 14. Peter encouraged Christians to endure suffering in such a way that the grace of God would be manifested in their lives. 15. He said that Christian suffering would last only for a while but the glory of Christ would be eternal. Previous

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Highlight the story of how the Israelites crossed the Red Sea.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State two lessons which Christians can learn from this incident

answer: HOW THE ISRAELITES CROSSED THE RED SEA. (EXODUS 14). i. After the ten plagues, Pharaoh allowed the Israelites to leave Egypt for the wilderness to worship their God. ii. Later, when Pharaoh realized that the Israelites had left for good, he regretted for allowing them to go. iii The Israelites were guarded by the Lord by a pillar of cloud during the day and pillar of fire by night. iv. Pharaoh quickly organized his soldiers and chariots to chase the Israelites with the hope of bringing them back. v. God allowed Pharaoh and his charioteers to pursue the Israelites in order to gain glory over the Egyptians. vi. They caught up with them at Pihahiroth where they had encamped in front of the sea. vii. When the Egyptians drew nearer, the Israelites became afraid and panicked/displaying lack of faith in God and Moses. vii. They cried to the Lord and began to accuse Moses for bringing them into the wilderness to die. ix. They said that they should have been left in Egypt to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness. x. Moses told them not to entertain any fear but to stand firm for the Lord would fight for them. xi. Moses again said that in no time they would not see the Egyptians again. xii. Moses then cried to God and he was told by God to stretch his rod over the sea. xii. After that, a great wind Came and drove back the waters. xiv. The Israelites passed through on dry land/ground. xv. The Egyptians gave them a hot chase, but the wheels of their chariots could not move xvi. Moses immediately stretched his rod over the sea and the waters returned leading to the drowning of the Egyptians. xvii. The people then came to believe in Yahweh and in Moses His servant. B. LESSONS TO BE LEARNT FROM THE CROSSING OF THE RED SEA İ. Need to have faith in God. ii. God is always ready to protect his people in time of crisis/ provide a Way of escape for his people. iii. God will never allow our enemies to overcome us. iv. God is faithful and reliable/ always loyal to his people. V. Need to be patient in times of trouble/ crisis. vi. Need to pray always in difficult times vii. Need to seek God at all times/ being obedient to God's word/command. vii. We should have trust in our leaders. ix. Leaders must be Confident always and inspire their followers to have same. x. Leaders should encourage their followers always in time of difficulty to stand firm and not panic. xi. God punishes those who do not believe in Him/humbles them. xii. God is sovereign/Can do the impossible. xiii. Fear and panic weaken our faith and cause us to speak evil against God and spiritual leaders

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: However, I will not tear away all the kingdom, but I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake David my servant.....Recount what led to the above pronouncement

answer: A. REASONS FOR THE PRONOUNCEMENT (1 KINGS 11:1-13) i. When Solomon had established himself as King of lsrael after his father David, he started loving many foreign women of whom God had warned him not to marry. ii. Those women included the daughter of Pharaoh and Moabite, Edomite, Sidonian and Hittite Women. iii. The reason was that they would surely turn away his heart after their gods. iv. Thus, during the latter part of Solomon's reign, his heart turned away from God who had appeared to him twice. V. This came about because he married many foreign wives against God's will. vi, He had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines and these women-led him astray. vii. Solomon built high places for the gods of his foreign wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods there, viii, He built high places for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, Molech the abomination. of Ammon, ix, God was angry with Solomon because his heart had turned away from the God of Israel. x. His marriage of foreign wives also led to the adulteration of the worship of Yahweh. xi. God was not pleased with Solomon, because he did not follow Him wholeheartedly as his father, David did. xi. God, therefore, decided to divide the Davidic Kingdom of Israel into two after the death of Solomon. xiii. The Lord said to Solomon "Since this has been your mind and you have not kept my Covenant and status which l have commanded you, I will surely tear the Kíngdom from you and give it to your servant". xiv. One tribe (Judah) was to be retained for the sake of David and for the sake of Jerusalem which Yahweh had chosen. Xv. Solomon who had previously been devoted to God backslid from the worship of God/His wives turned away his heart after other gods. xvi. Solomon was however assured that for the sake of his father David, the prophecy would not happen during his days but during the days of his son. Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Outline Nehemiah's immediate reactions to the news about the state of affairs in Jerusalem

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Identify three virtues that can be learnt from Nehemiah's reactions

answer: A) HOW NEHEMIAH REACTED TO THE NEWS ABOUT THE STATE OF AFFAIRS IN JERUSALEM (NEHEMIAH 1:2-11) i. Nehemiah was one of the Jews taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar ii. He was made a CUp-bearer to the king of Persia in Susa. iii. One day, Nehemiah was in Susa when a delegation led by his brother Hanani came to him with men from Judah. iv. Nehemiah asked them concerning the few Jews who were still in Jerusalem and about the city itself. v. Hanani made him aware that the people in Jerusalem were in great trouble and shame. vi. He further said that the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and its gates destroyed by fire. vii. Upon hearing that, Nehemiah broke down, wept, mourned and fasted for days. viii. Nehemiah prayed to God to hear the prayer of his servants ix. He confessed that He and his father's house had sinned. x. Again, he Confessed that they had not kept the commandments, statutes and ordinances Moses commanded. xi. He asked God to remember His words to Moses that if they were unfaithful he would scatter them among the people. xii. But should they repent and keep His commandment, He would gather them and restore them to the place He has chosen for them xiii. He reminded God that He had redeemed His people by His great power. xiv. He finally petitioned God to listen to His servant and grant him success and mercy. xv. After the prayer, God intervened and touched the heart of the king to grant him mercy, to visit his people. B. VIRTUES THAT CAN BE LEARNT FROM NEHEMIAH'S REACTION i. Nehemiah was patriotic; hence, we need to learn to show patriotism/ love our nation. ii. He was very prayerful. We need to emulate Nehemiah and be prayerful. iii. He was conscious of the sins Committed by him and his fellow Jews; so he confessed to God/ There is the need for a country to accept her sins and confession. iV. There is the need for national repentance. V. It is important to have faith in God/God is faithful. vi. We should always intercede for our nation/ pray for the well-being of our country. vii. There is the need to be focused/ committed. vii. We should have vision and share it with others. ix. We should be sincere to God by confessing our sins. x. We should show empathy with the plight of our people/selfless. xi. We should demonstrate humility and sincere service. Previous Next

questionText: SECTION A: THEMES FROM THE OLD TESTAMENT

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: l am no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I am a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore trees...give an account of the events that led to this statement.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: ldentify three reasons for which people complain about the activities of some men of God today.

answer: A. AMOS' ENCOUNTER WITH AMAZIAH (AMOS 7:10-17) i. Amos was a shepherd in Judah whom God called to prophesy in Israel. ii. He spoke against the social and religious malpractices of the Israelites of his day. iii. Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, reported Amos to the king of Israel, Jeroboam l, accusing him of conspiracy and treason. iv. According to Amaziah, Amos had prophesied that the king of Israel would go into exile. v. Amaziah then met Amos who had told him that he was forbidden to speak against the king and the temple. vi, Amaziah misconstrued Amos for one of the many false prophets of the time and called him a seer (a professional prophet who prophesies for a living). vi. Amaziah commanded Amos to return to Judah, his home town to prophesy and earn a living there and never again at Bethel. vii. This was because Bethel was the King's sanctuary and the temple of the kingdom. ix. Amos disassociated himself from the wrong impression created about him by Amaziah. x. He told Amaziah that the Lord called him to prophesy in Israel while he was tending his flock and dressing the sycamore trees. xi. And for challenging him, Amos told Amaziah that his wife would become a harlot in the city and his sons shall fall by the sword and he Amaziah would die in exile. B.WHY PEOPLE COMPLAIN ABOUT THE ACTIVITIES OF SOME MEN OF GOD i. Use of occultic/magical powers. ii. Commercialisation of the gospel/extortion. iii. Discrimination against the p0or and underprivileged. iv. Immorality/ immoral lives. v. False doctrines. vi. False prophecies/ not trustworthy. vii. Lack of adequate education. vii. Embezzlement/ misappropriation of funds. ix. Over-emphasis on prosperity messages above salvation and redemption. x. Political alignment. xi. Display of wealth and opulence. xi. questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES '

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Relate the trial of Jesus before the Sanhedrin according to Mark's gospel.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: Give two reasons for which people bear false witness against others.

answer: A. THE TRIAL OF JESUS BEFORE THE ŠANHEDRIN ACCORDING TO MARK (MARK 14:53-65) i. After Jesus was arrested in the garden of Gethsemane, Peter followed at a distance into the courtyard of the high priest and there warmed himself at the fire. ii. The Sanhedrin sought false testimony against Jesus to put him to death but they found none. iii. The Sanhedrin was a body of religious leaders presided by the high priest. iv. Many people came to give false evidence against him but their statements did not tally. v. But finally, in accordance 1lse with Jewish law, two witnesses came forward and accused Jesus of saying that he would destroy the temple Jon in Jerusalem and in three days build another. vi. The temple stood as the centre of Judaism; thus, Jesus was attacking the heart of the Jewish religion. vii. The high priest then asked Jesus under oath whether he was the Messiah, the son of the Blessed One. vii. Jesus replied affirmatively that he was the Messiah. ix. He also said that they would see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of power and coming with the clouds of heaven. x. The high priest then tore his garment as a sign of righteous indignation and asked if they needed a further evidence against this blasphemy. xi. According to the high priest, Jesus had spoken blasphemy, so, he sought to the decision of the council. xii. The whole council condemned Jesus and said that he deserved death as a ber penalty for blasphemy. xiii. Eventually, some members of the Sanhedrin spat on him, while others covered his face and struck him to express their contempt and hate for his Messianic claims. xiv. They asked Jesus to prophesy and mention the one who struck him. xv. The guards likewise gave him some blows B. REASONS WHY PEOPLE BEAR FALSE WITNESS AGAINST OTHERS İ. Hatred/character assassination/ defamation ii. Envy/ jealousy iii. Greed iv. Vengeance/ retribution v. Bribery/monetary gains vi. To win favour vi. Religious/tribal /filial reasons vii. Coercion/ force ix. Out of fear x. For selfish interest xi. To incriminate eliminate Previous Next

subject: Christian Religious Studies
questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: My soul is very sorrowful, even to death; remain here and watch with me. Give an account of what happened to Jesus after he made this statement.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: identify two ways by which one can assist a fellow Christian going through challenges

answer: A. JESUS' AGONY AND ARREST IN THE GARDEN OF GETHSEMANE (MATTHEW 26:36-56) i. Jesus and his disciples went to the garden of Gethsemane to pray. ii. He took with him Peter, James and John (member of his inner circle) to another place, leaving the rest behind. iii. Jesus then left the three and went further to pray alone. iv. He became greatly distressed and made the above statement. v. He then went a little farther on and fell tọ the ground to pray, saying my father if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; neverthless God's will should be done vi. This prayer shows the profound humanity of Jesus and his resolute courage and submission to the will of God. vii. The cup in this context is a symbol or deep sorrow and suffering. viii. Jesus came back to the three, Peter, James and John found them sleeping and he asked Peter whether they could not watch with him for one hour. ix. Jesus then told them to watch and pray so that they would not enter into temptation. x. He said the spirit is willing but the body is weak. xi. This means that though the disciples had the best of intentions, the weakness of the flesh failed them. xii. Again, for the second time, Jesus went away to pray and he again asked that if it was possible the cup should pass by him. xii. Jesus came back and found the three disciples asleep again xiv. Jesus left them and went to pray for the third time and he came back to meet the disciples still asleep. xv. He asked them whether they were still sleeping and taking their rest. Xvi. Jesus then told them that the hour was at hand and the Son of Man would be betrayed into the hands of sinners. xvi. He made them aware that the betrayer was at hand so they should get ready to go. xvii. As Jesus was speaking,. Judas Iscariot led a crowd with swords and clubs to arrest him. xix. But one of these who stood by drew his sword and cut the ear of the high priest's slave but Jesus restrained him. xx. The crowd then arrested Jesus after Judas had kissed him. xxi. They led Him to the high priest's house, for the Jewish trial. B. WAYS BY WHICH ONE GOING THROUGH CHALLENGES CAN BE ASSISTED i. Visiting the one going through the challenges. ii. Praying with the person having the problem. iii. Assisting the person in cash or in-kind when necessary/ sharing your resources with him or her. iv. Counselling the victim/ providing advice. v. Relocating the victim/ changing victim's environment. vi. Seeking redress/justice. vii. Speaking on their behalf advocacy. vii. Encouraging the person to trust in God. ix. Show love/empathy. questionText: THEMES FROM THE SYNOPTIC GOSPELS AND THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Give an account of Stephen's defence before the Sanhedrin.

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: State three lessons that can be learnt from Stephen's defence.

answer: STEPHEN'S DEFENCĚ BEFORE THE SANHEDRIN (ACT6: 2-6; 8-9 7:1-10) i. Stephen was one of the seven deacons appointed to be in charge of the welfare of the poor and needy in the early church. ii. He was full of faith, grace and power and performed great wonders and signs among the people. iii. Some of the Jews argued with Stephen but they could not withstand the wisdom and the spirit with which he spoke. iv. They instigated some men who accused Stephen of speaking blasphemous words against God and Moses. v Specifically, that Jesus of Nazareth would destroy the temple, and change the customs which Moses delivered to them. vi. By Jewish law, the accusations leveled against Stephen constituted serious offence punishable by death. vii. In his defence, Stephen tried to prove that even in the past, God did not confine His presence to the temple at Jerusalem. viii. He decided to trace the history of the Jews to show that God is universal and does not only dwell in the temple. ix. He cited the example of how God appeared to Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia and asked him to go and live in Haran and Abraham obeyed. x. He stressed that God told Abraham that his descendants would become slaves in another country where they would be maltreated for four hundred years xi. But God would punish that nation which enslaved them and later Abraham's decendants would go out and Worship him in the land of Canaan. Xii. Again, Stephen said that God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision and when he became the father of Isaac, he circumcised him on the eighth day. xii. Isaac also became the father of Jacob and Jacob became the father of the patriarchs. xiv. The Patriarchs were jealous of Jacob and sold him into Egypt. xv. God was with Joseph and rescued him from all afflictions. B.LESSONS TÖ BE LEARNT FROM STEPHEN'S DEFENCE I. We should be bold and courageous when we face trials. ii. We should have strong faith in God. iii. In times of persecution, we should rely on God to defend us iv When God blesses us, the enemy cannot overcome us v There is the need to remember our history vi bearing false witness destroys one's personality/ integrity vii To obtain protection against the devil. we should always pray. viii. We should be prepared to defend our faith even when we face opposition ix We should forgive those who hurt us. x. We should be bold to spread the gospel. xi We should be knowledgeable in scriptures. xii. We should be respectful to elders. Previous Next

questionText: SECTION C: THEMES FROM SELECTED EPISTLES

subQuestions.label: a
subQuestions.text: Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed... What other teachings did James give on effective prayer?

subQuestions.label: b
subQuestions.text: In what three ways are Christians misusing prayers today?

answer: A. JAMES' TEACHING ON EFFECTIVE PRAYER(JAMES 1:2-8; 5:13-18) i To James, effective prayer is one that God answers. ii. And to achieve this, one needs to repent and confess one's sins to God and to one another in order to attract God's healing and forgiveness of sin, iii James encouraged Christians to count it all joy whenever they meet trials. iv. He says when one's faith is tested through trials, one becomes steadfast and later becomes perfect and complete. v. According to James, if anyone lacks wisdom, he should ask God in prayer and he would have it generously. vi. James holds the view that one must pray in faith without doubting Vil. For anyone who doubts is like a wave of the sea that is driven and tossed by the wind. vii. And that, a person who doubts will receive nothing from the Lord. ix. He again said that if anyone is indisposed, he should call upon the elders of the church to anoint him with oil and pray in humility,. x. And that, the prayer of faith will heal the sick. xi. James revealed that God is glorified when people pray for the right things. xii. Thus, prayer should be made according to the will of God. xii. James urged Christians to pray in humility. XiV. Christians should be persistent in prayer by praying unceasingly till their requests are met xv. James is of the opinion that the fervent prayer of the righteous has a great effect xvi. He gave an example of Elijah who prayed fervently for no rain and there was no rain for three and half years. Xvii. And after three and half years, he prayed again and there was rain B. HOW PRAYERS ARE MISUSED BY CHRISTIANS TODAY İ Paying money for prayers/ consultation fee for prayers/ Commercialisation of prayers. ii. Cursing people in prayers/ praying against enemies. iii Praying at the wrong time when they should be working/substituting prayer for work. iv. Shouting making noise to disturb others. v. Prayers for the highest donor/ bidders. vi. Substituting prayers for righteousness. vii. Praying with selfish motives. viii. Praying not in accordance with the word/will of God. ix. idolatry in prayer/praying to religious leaders rather than God. X. Effectiveness of prayer wrongly associated with material objects, e.g. salt candle, stickers, anointing oil, etc. Previous Next
